articles.title: Beyond the Margins Walkthrough - Crimson Desert Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Beyond the Margins is the first main story quest in the Charting the Unknown DLC for Crimson Desert. Kliff contemplates what to do with his life now that all
articles.body:
Beyond the Margins is the first main story quest in the Charting the Unknown DLC for Crimson Desert . Kliff contemplates what to do with his life now that all his fellow Greymanes are at peace and having a good time. Before he can settle down, this leads to a new incoming threat via an ominous sandstorm. This IGN guide covers how to complete all 13 subquests within Beyond the Margins. Click the links below to jump straight to our dedicated walkthroughs:

After completing the original main questline and finishing Epilogue: Journey's End , you'll have access to this new questline. While playing as Kliff, head over to the Pailune tavern where you'll immediately trigger a cutscene. You'll find many familiar Greymanes having a good time together and gambling inside.

Once Kliff has finished appreciating his comrades having a good time, he heads outside to search for Oongka. This leads to a fishing trip as the two of you wander up the road . While it is a slow walk, you won't have to travel too far since a cutscene will transport you the rest of the way.

Once the cutscene ends, you'll be trapped at the river until you successfully catch a fish . This part may be finicky, as we were unable to get any fish to bite when casting far from the pier. Meanwhile, casting a short distance in front of Kliff led to an almost immediate bite.

After catching a fish, a cutscene will start that leads to A Moment's Respite completing. For the next quest, Familiar Faces, return to Pailune and search for a couple of Greymanes with a message.

Back in Pailune, Familiar Faces brings you to the east side along the docks. You'll find two Greymanes not too far from the nearby barber. Start a conversation with Andrew to learn that a freesword named Matthias is looking for Kliff. You may remember them from Chapter 2, during Hernand in Chaos . Once your chat ends here, you'll get the quest reward despite it not being over yet. It's a Greymane Apprentice Combat Armor, upgraded to level 3.

Continuing from here sends you to the Pailune Castle on the northeast side of town. Make sure you're ready for a boss fight, as you won't have a chance to prepare before the upcoming cutscene. As you get close to the castle, you'll encounter Matthias waiting on the steps ahead in his full suit of armor. This leads to a friendly rematch in a small fighting area.

Once you chat with Matthias, be ready for Crimson Desert to continue its pattern of cheap attacks. Before you have a good chance to recover from the cutscene, he'll fire off a flurry of attacks at you. With that said, you can expect a much tougher boss fight compared to the first time . But at least you now have more skills to take advantage of, and he only has one health bar now. Here are some tips for fighting Matthias:

Now that you're deep in Crimson Desert, Matthias has adopted the same aggressive mobility that many bosses have. This forces you to use a lot of stamina to avoid his combos before getting a chance to respond.

On top of his ability to dodge frequently and close gaps, his attack animations are much quicker now too. Until you get a decent read of them, you can rely on the classic Focused Insight skill to slow time down. This works on many bosses to help you dodge or parry incoming attacks.

You can still manhandle Matthias with skills like Scissor Takedown, but you'll have a small window to follow up.

The main powerful attack to watch out for is when the area darkens, Matthias lifts his sword, and it begins glowing. A ring around him will pulse as it expands farther away from him. It may seem like you can stay outside its range, but this can be deceiving. The better move is to use your Aerial Force Palm to fly above it.

A strong strategy for many bosses in Crimson Desert is to rely on Force Palm punches to fill their stagger bar. These have a decent range that, when upgraded, can combo into a small stun. Using Force Palm punches with other attacks like strong Forward Slashes can be powerful. You just need to make sure not to overextend since most bosses will only take so much of a beating before recovering regardless.

Once you've filled Matthias's stagger bar, you can get a couple of hits in before landing a finisher. As previously mentioned, don't forget to use Focused Insight if you're having trouble dealing with his mobility. And of course, bring food to heal during the battle.

After defeating Matthias, a cutscene will begin where he decides to become a Greymane. While Kliff is a bit hesitant, this introduces a new feature of Honorary Greymanes you can use. Return to your Greymane comrades on the west side of Pailune to complete Familiar Faces. You'll find Jijeong Monks with a message from the head monk requesting your presence. This leads to the next quest, Teachings to Light the Way.

Teachings to Light the Way brings you to the Jijeong Temple , far south-southeast of Pailune, past Demeniss. This places it west of Delesyia, near the Serpent Marsh. Make your way there to trigger a cutscene with the Chief monk inside the temple. After some small talk, they explain that T'rukan is harassing people in his chase for true power.

The Chief Monk then asks that you teach them a lesson again, after having done it once before in Chapter 9 . Once you've finished speaking with them, head a little northeast toward the Bamboo Forest where you'll find T'rukan. As you may expect, this leads into a boss fight, so make sure you're ready to go. We recommend stocking up on food since you'll be down a weapon for this encounter.

Once you approach T'rukan, he explains that you only succeeded against him due to being armed to the teeth. This leads to Kliff challenging him with a tree branch. As goes with any boss fight in Crimson Desert, be prepared for an attack almost immediately as the cutscene ends. Your UI, such as your health bar and other icons, won't even be visible yet.

If you remember the previous fight with T'rukan , it's very similar, despite some combos now having an extra attack. This means it's more important than ever to have enough stamina for dodging and blocking. With that said, we've included some of T'rukan's major attacks below:

As with the original fight, T'rukan telegraphs many of his attacks with a purple energy. This time around, it's emphasized even more. However, only certain attacks have a delay, allowing you to see them coming.

T'rukan frequently charges toward you for rapid punch combos that you may be able to parry if you're quick enough.

T'rukan has a strong attack that is heavily telegraphed, giving you an opportunity to run away. He'll become surrounded by that purple energy, while also summoning three large spirit animals nearby. After a moment, they'll all charge toward you simultaneously. Don't bother trying to hit him since you won't be able to while he's charging up.

Similar to the first fight, T'rukan can send purple projectiles at you, but he'll do it more frequently now. You can use Nature's Snare to catch them and then fling them back. Make sure not to wait too long after catching them, since he can melee you out of holding them.

While Focused Insight is often a strong skill for slowing down a boss fight, you may struggle to take advantage of it here. This is primarily due to his projectiles that you won't have a button prompt to react to.

T'rukan's powerful attack is telegraphed by the area darkening as he moves his glowing purple hands in a circle. After a short delay, he'll shoot three purple projectiles and then charge toward you. This isn't new to the second encounter, but he will throw a second punch upon reaching you. We don't recommend trying to use Nature's Snare on the projectiles here since he follows up quickly after them.

The toughest part of fighting T'rukan aside from not having your weapon is how relentless he is. He's rarely vulnerable between attacks since he consistently follows them up with more. While you don't have your weapon, you will still benefit from Abyss Gear attached to your gloves and armor. This is where certain Abyss Gear, like Slashing Reeds, can deal damage upon dodging when being hit.

But if you don't want to rely on your tree branch for the whole fight, you can use spirit attacks like Force Palm punches . These are a consistent way to deal damage while filling his stagger bar. Once you've beaten T'rukan a second time, you can return to the Chief Monk to finish up the quest.

While chatting with the Chief Monk, they mention that there's another problem for you to look into. The Eastern Witches spoke with the monk about whispers of darkness in the desert. Which they explain that Antumbra Order followers may be after for power. Before you can chase them down, you'll need to find a friend in Varnia to help map the way. This completes Teachings to Light the Way and leads into Where Rumors Gather.

Where Rumors Gather sends you to Varnia to track down a mapmaker for help. You'll need to ask around to see if you can learn where Sebastian is. Once you've found him and gotten him to help you, you'll go for a short trip that turns into an enlightening cutscene. This finishes both Where Rumors Gather and even the next quest below, Witches of the East.

Witches of the East starts and completes during the cutscene that triggers at the end of Where Rumors Gather. Therefore, you don't actually have to do anything for this one. You will, however, get a useful reward for exploring the desert in the coming quests, 100 Glowing Seeds.

Beyond the Sandstorm starts by teaching you to use Marker Stones and Glowing Seeds to travel the sandstorm. This is because you won't be able to use your minimap, main map, or even cardinal directions via your compass. Marker Stones have yellow beams that point toward others that eventually lead to villages. You can examine a plate on each Marker Stone to see where it goes.

Glowing Seeds mainly function as breadcrumbs to keep track of where you are and to see them with your lantern. Placing one at a Marker Stone is a good way to find them if you get lost. However, you will eventually run into Corrupted Marker Stones that point in the wrong direction. As part of the Distorted Light quest, you'll need to purify them.

The main goal of Beyond the Sandstorm is to discover quests hidden inside the storm while purifying Corrupted Marker Stones. You'll need to track down the following four quests:

Once you've finished those four and Distorted Light, Beyond the Sandstorm will also be complete. This leads into the next quest much farther down, Veil of Darkness.

Spoilers For Where Each Hidden Village Inside the Sandstorm Is

If you'd like to see where every sandstorm village is so you can find their relevant quests, we've included the map below. While inside the sandstorm, it can be difficult to figure out where you are, but there are helpful tricks.

Using the map, you can often find each village by starting outside the storm or inside a village to see where you are. You can then point yourself in the correct direction to find it. Otherwise, you'll need to rely on the Marker Stones.

Distorted Light focuses on purifying Corrupted Marker Stones around the sandstorm. You'll know something is wrong with it if you see a purple sludge seeping out of it. On top of this, you'll likely run into enemies near them as well. A good way to deal with the Antumbra enemies is to use Nature's Snare to catch and reflect their projectiles. Otherwise, to purify a Corrupted Marker Stone, you'll need to pull out multiple dark stakes from the surrounding area.

The strategy to find them as hinted in-game, is to use your Blinding Flash skill. While reflecting the sun, you should see dark purple beams, similar to the bright yellow ones from a Marker Stone. However, we've had mixed success with them actually appearing. Therefore, you can try circling the area around the Corrupted Marker Stone to find them.

Dark stakes appear as small pillars sticking out of the ground. While they can be out in the open, they're more likely to be somewhat hidden. For example, they can be hidden inside ruins, hidden inside a tree, or surrounded by Bismuth ore.

Where to Find All Five Corrupted Marker Stones in Distorted Light

It's easy to get lost in the sandstorm, which can make it especially hard to track down the Corrupted Marker Stones. If you're unsure of where to find them, we've included all five on the map below. The locations aren't exact, but they're close enough to give you a good idea of where to search.

If you'd like to keep track of the ones you've purified, you can use the checkboxes below:

Once you've purified all five Corrupted Marker Stones, return to Sebastian near the southern side of the sandstorm. This triggers a cutscene where he realizes that all of the Corrupted Marker Stones were pointing to a specific unknown location. Follow the next quest, Veil of Darkness, to investigate that spot.

The Missing Calf is one of four quests you can discover in the sandstorm. Upon reaching the village of Hazran , on the west-southwest side of the zone, this quest will appear. Speak with a group of four villagers there to learn that their bison herd was lost in the storm. Despite them not mentioning it in this cutscene, your goal is to recover one bison calf.

Once the cutscene ends, look down the nearby steps toward the ranch. Then, aim your lantern at the path to find a yellow streak flowing through the air . By now in Crimson Desert, you'll have used this mechanic before for certain quests, so it may seem familiar.

Follow the yellow streak until you reach a spot with some Antumbra enemies and, of course, a bison calf casually wandering the area. While dealing with those pesky enemies, you won't have to worry about hitting the calf since you can't. Once it's safe enough, pick up the bison calf and return to Hazran.

If you leave the ruins here by going out from the front right corner, with the big slab wall behind you, this will lead you toward the village. You'll eventually hit a wall that you can follow with it on your left to reach the village. Otherwise, you can drop the calf for a brief moment to use your lantern and follow the yellow streak back.

Upon arriving at the village, enter the fenced ranch and bring the calf to the same guy from earlier . He still has the same orange turban on from before. Once your cutscene is finished here, return to Sebastian near the south side of the storm. Approaching the map near him will complete The Missing Calf.

The Buried Neighbors is one of four quests you can find in the sandstorm. This one starts at the village of Lukumiya , near the southwest side of the sandstorm. You can also head west from where Sebastian is to get there. While near Sebastian, you'll still have access to your compass for directions. Otherwise, you can use the Marker Stones to find the village.

Speak with a coughing villager inside the objective area to learn about the plague hitting Lukumiya. You'll learn that they've run out of medicine and that nobody has been able to get more. The villager believes the neighboring village has turned against them due to the plague. In an attempt to help them, they direct you toward the village to get more medicine.

Their clues say to go past a dry well behind the village and then head northeast. In our experience, we weren't able to find that dry well and instead went northeast from Lukumiya . This takes you toward the village of Maddin near the center of the storm. As you get closer, keep an eye out for Marker Stones that you can examine to see where Maddin is.

Once you arrive in Maddin, speak to the Apothecary up some stairs there. You'll learn that they assumed the villagers in Lukumiya were angry with them. This leads to a misunderstanding that Kliff clears up. After the conversation ends, return to Lukumiya with the medicine and speak to the villager near the well. Then, you can return to Sebastian near the south side of the storm to complete The Buried Neighbors.

Village in Darkness is one of four quests you can find in the sandstorm. Unlike the other three, this one simply revolves around liberating a village . After clearing enough enemies out of Yasmin , near the northwest side of the storm, you can return to Sebastian .

As mentioned in other sections, you'll find him near the south side of the storm. Once you've finished updating the map near Sebastian, Village in Darkness is complete.

The Lost Child is one of four quests you can discover inside the sandstorm. This one is a bit harder to find compared to the others since it doesn't start inside a village. You'll instead need to track down the missing child at a Marker Stone between the villages Maddin and Faraj . Maddin is near the center, while Faraj is near the east side of the storm.

Once you find the child leaning against the Marker Stone, talk to them to trigger a cutscene. They'll explain that something is wrong with the Marker Stones, as many quests here also mention. After the cutscene ends, follow the Marker Stones and escort them to Faraj . As long as you carefully avoid quicksand, you can call a horse and have the child ride with you.

Shortly after arriving in Faraj, a cutscene will show the boy reuniting with his parents. You can then return to Sebastian near the south side of the storm to complete The Lost Child.

articles.title: The Resident Evil: Biohazard Unleashed Bundle From Humble Includes 9 Capcom Classics for $40
articles.summary: Humble Bundle's latest drop of PC games is a Resident Evil: Biohazard Unleashed bundle, featuring 9 games from Capcom's series that you can snag for your Steam library for as low as $40.
articles.body:
If you're longing for more Resident Evil after playing Resident Evil Requiem this year or catching Zach Cregger’s new movie , Humble Bundle is here to make your day with its Resident Evil: Biohazard Unleashed bundle . This features a stacked lineup of 9 PC games from Capcom's series - including the Resident Evil HD Remaster , Resident Evil 2 remake, Resident Evil Village , and more - that you can add to your Steam library for as low as $40.

Humble Bundle – Resident Evil: Biohazard Unleashed Bundle

To put into perspective how excellent this offer is, the grand total of all these games would normally cost you $289 if you bought them all individually, so you're saving an incredible amount. Plus, if you want to pay more than $40, you can give a little extra cash to Humble, publishers, and to a charity (of which this bundle's is the Raiden Science Foundation ).

Dropping below that $40 mark won't get you the full 9 games from the list above, but you'll still get a small selection. If you go to $26, this gets you 5 games (RE 4 HD, RE 5 Gold Edition, RE 6 Complete, RE 7 biohazard Gold Edition, and RE Village Gold Edition), while dropping to $18 only gets you 2 games (biohazard and Village). The lowest point you can go to is $10, but that only gets you Village, so you're missing out on quite a few iconic titles.

If you're hoping to grab this Resident Evil lineup for your Steam library, the clock is ticking to do so. As of the time of writing, Humble's main page for this bundle says it's only available for 27 more days, so you've got about a month to scoop it up. The page also highlights that these keys can expire, so make sure to redeem and activate them on Steam before June 2nd next year.

Hannah Hoolihan is a freelancer who writes with the commerce team here at IGN.

articles.title: Want a New Elder Scrolls? Play Queen's Domain | IGN Quick Review
articles.summary: Queen's Domain is a pixelated, first-person, and tough as nails throwback fantasy RPG that's worth the effort.
articles.body:
I'm a sucker for a good throwback to the early polygonal 32-bit era – Mouthwashing, Signalis, Crow Country, and Boltgun 2 are some recent favorites that come to mind. The latest one I've locked in on is Queen's Domain, a fantasy RPG that's as if an Elder Scrolls game was made for the PlayStation 1. Actually, it's explicitly inspired by FromSoftware's pre-Dark Souls series King's Field, where slow, deliberate first-person combat and exploration complemented punishing difficulty (which would later become FromSoft's signature, of course). But as much as Queen's Domain draws clear inspiration or shares similarities, it's a singular experience in 2026 that, so far, wields the intended friction of an old-school game wonderfully.

Washed ashore on a jungle island after your ship is sucked through the sea by a demonic queen, you're alone and in danger. Human-sized lady bugs and crickets lunge at you and follow you around, and the only thing you have to defend yourself in the early minutes is a rusted sword offered by a few survivors. Combat is tedious in these opening moments; avoid crickets by backpedaling when their animation starts, circle-strafe bugs when their wings flutter, and bunnyhop to hopefully avoid lasers shooting from those pesky eye plants stuck to the walls (which can shoot at you from a mile away). It's not an enticing or inviting start, but I had faith I'd strike a pile of gems if I just kept digging.

There are no quest markers, waypoints, or highlighted paths, just a rounded compass pulled straight out of King's Field. As someone who loves less handholding in exploration, I felt an obligation to see if Queen's Domain was doing this design philosophy justice. So, I pushed forward slowly, facing each enemy and navigating the tropical ruins carefully, waiting for a breakthrough as everything from resurrected skeletons to dragonflies wanted to kill me.

With just a faint glint on an off-shore mound, I found a belt of throwing knives to add to my measly arsenal. Important items are quite hard to identify in the world since they blend into the pixelated art style, so it took me longer than I'd like to admit to find these knives. Cool, I can finally kill those annoying eye plants, and also hit deep-seated switches next to big stone doors; one as a shortcut back to a save point and one to an underground crypt. You're not told to do any of this, but with enough poking and prodding at the world itself, you make these kinds of discoveries naturally.

Along the way, I picked up a spear that does piercing damage and a wooden club to do blunt damage, both of which complement the slash damage of my rusted sword – which I'd also leveled up in proficiency just from using it. Now the weapon triangle came into focus: each enemy is weak, neutral, or resistant to different damage types, so weapon switching became part of the plodding combat dance. I should also mention that stamina is the biggest factor in damage output – each attack depletes the stamina bar, and the more stamina you have in store, the more damage you do. It recovers quickly, but you can't just spam attacks to get through enemies, which further emphasizes a calculated approach to combat.

In the underground crypt I mentioned, things started to flow smoother as I understood this dynamic and got better at reacting to attack patterns. Enemies are designed to be primitive in the spirit of old games, with one-note attacks and predictable behaviors, and it's when you have to juggle multiple enemies where the more interesting challenge comes in. With the club's alternate attack, I could lunge at skeletons and get out of the way before they do their own lunging stab, and charging up my primary attack meant I could clear crickets in fewer swipes.

Since there are no autosaves and death means losing precious progress (save points are deliberately infrequent), finding a gate key at the end of the crypt raised the tension even further – now, I just needed to survive to make it back to my lone save point. This is another old-school design decision that, while it can be frustrating, complements Queen's Domain’s world design and the overall way it approaches challenge.

The key opened a gate back on a pier along the shore, which then led to a closed arena for the first real boss fight. I saw the screen-wide health bar pop up, and damn . The skeletal Shrine Guardian was bigger and more aggressive than anything before it, and caused knockdown with charged up sword slashes. Escaping its range was the toughest part and I got my ass beat the first try, but…aha! The spear's alternate attack is also a super-fast backdash, so what if I baited the boss and backdash-attacked, and then unloaded throwing knives while kiting it as I waited for my stamina to recover? Light work.

This highlighted the importance of alternate attacks, and defeating it rewarded me with a new, pristine holy sword with an alt attack that lets you briefly glide through the air. Sweet – higher damage, cooler looking, and a new way to explore… hold up, this opens up so many pathways I thought inaccessible! A broken bridge led to an important discovery for the main quest, as well as a new magic torch weapon; tree branches acting as platforms led to an area where I'd fight through waves of skeletons and bugs, and then use my magic torch to light up a tower needed to progress. Cryptic scriptures would poke at my curiosity about the world and lead me forward without outright telling me, and cracks in the sides of broken buildings contained actual rewards and key items like an airdash upgrade.

If I had to point to one thing I think is genius about Queen's Domain, it's the way its level design naturally guides you in exploration. In the absence of a map, you have to rely on examining the world for visual cues and remembering its layout. You'll need to commit to memory the areas you haven't fully explored and which paths you should return to after unlocking something new. What you're fundamentally asked to do isn't groundbreaking, but how it puts the onus on you to figure things out makes the experience so much more interesting.

Consumable healing items are scarce early on, and resting at save points respawns enemies – it's dangerous out there, and heading out to hopefully make progress is daunting. Issues like getting caught on geometry during attacks can be infuriating when survival is at stake, and some enemy types are just tedious to handle. A few frustrations can chip at my enthusiasm, but I'm willing to wade through those rougher waters because within these seemingly antiquated design principles is an RPG that's oddly refreshing and satisfying.

Moment-to-moment pacing changed quite a bit throughout the Water Temple area, which I cleared at about six hours into my playthrough. The dungeon crawling itself was paced really well; I never felt lost and the layout balanced being intuitive and provoking curiosity. It already dawned on me that this had a metroidvania edge with expanded abilities opening new paths forward; that much was clear when I got a second airdash upgrade here to cross a huge gap to make it to the last leg of the dungeon. I got a lot more comfortable with combat, feeling loosened up with a growing arsenal that included a dual damage-type morning star and the magic torch's fireballs. Even then, it contained some tough battles against poisonous sea creatures and pincer bugs throughout this lengthy dungeon, still requiring careful approaches informed by using your limited capabilities in smart ways – which would be further tested in the dungeon's boss fight against a corrupted king whale who spawned adds and crashed waves of poison water.

Emerging from the sewers afterward and lighting another tower, I found a teleporter that also indicated that I had at least eight more areas ahead. Now, I could firmly grasp the scope of Queen's Domain, and as I approached the next area, the cursed and spiraling library of the Tower of Knowledge, I felt this adventure was going to get deeper. But it's one where I was going to grow with it, evident in the way I took down its door boss, the Skeletal Executioner, with nary a scratch by dodging its axe projectiles, casting my torch, and charging my holy sword. I've entered a flow state.

Part of me is thinking about how it can keep up the momentum, handle power scaling, and evolve in ways that'll continue to surprise. From scavenging ancient coins for slicker weapons and charms to boost stats, those little rewards have been nice to chew on. Walking into a new region piques my curiosity as much as it instills an unsettling vibe, both intrigued and scared of what new enemies lie ahead. Each bit of progress showed me something new and built me up as a player in ways that weren't just leveling and a stat sheet.

What I thought was a straightforward homage to generations passed has so far been a smart twist on an old-school RPG experience. Queen's Domain is modernized in a way that doesn't compromise its adherence to being a tough, sometimes obtuse, throwback.

Audio design has been key in building atmosphere and complementing the pseudo-PS1 aesthetic, too. The crackling of fires are as detailed as the retro-sounding battle cries of enemies, footsteps having me checking corners and turning around just in case, and the not-so-fantasy but fittingly lo-fi soundtrack got some earworms I'm humming along to as I write this. This all may seem gimmicky on the surface, but there's intentional design that makes it stand out from so many retro-inspired games. (You can also smooth out the pixelated look if you want, but I'd argue it's necessary).

Yes, I know it's not an expansive open world with reactive NPCs, branching quests, and dialogue choices, but Queen's Domain is scratching that itch for first-person fantasy RPG combat that you'd get from Elder Scrolls. It's got some fantastic dungeon crawling and it’s also an interesting way to look back and better understand what King's Field was trying to do all those years ago through something palatable in the modern era. And these opening hours are illustrative of how smart level design and a good bit of friction can make for unique experience that still has more beneath the surface.

It's been a hard-earned six hours, and there's so much more to see. If the bestiary is anything to go by, I've only encountered about 40 of the 188 enemies in Queen's Domain. This is going to be a long journey, but it's one I'm going to stay on until the wheels fall off. The thing I'm keeping in mind is if there's a deeper game underneath when the novelty wears off, and if it can sustain the sense of wonder it has delivered so far. Of course, this is not a full review since this seems to be a massive game, but Queen’s Domain has the makings of a sleeper hit.

articles.title: Highlander: The Original Screenplay Issue 1 - Official Trailer - IGN
articles.summary: Check out the trailer for Highlander: The Original Screenplay Issue 1, an upcoming comic based on the original story by writer Gregory Widen. Written by Gregory Widen, creator and screenwriter of the original Highlander movie, with art by Szymon Kudranski, the Highlander: The Original Screenplay comic series is based on Gregory Widen’s original script and reveals the original vision behind the timeless classic. The comic tells the story of the immortal Connor MacLeod as he lives through the centuries facing off against rivals for the mysterious prize. articles.title: Mass Effect Is Dead, But the Official Bioware Store Is Still Releasing New Merch for N7 Day
articles.body:
Wounds are still fresh coming into this year’s N7 Day, a day traditionally dedicated to celebrating Mass Effect’s history and announcing updates about its future. The festivities are now shrouded by the news of Bioware’s closure and the worst possible update for any franchise: the cancellation of Mass Effect 5.

Given how recently EA announced the studio shakeup, it stands to reason that Bioware had already prepared at least something for the N7 Day festivities. Some of these plans are still coming to fruition. Namely, a merch drop, including a new and improved version of the wearable N7 LED helmet .

Mass Effect N7 Wearable LED Helmet Images

The new helmet is a wearable replica of Shepard’s helmet from Mass Effect 3. It’s essentially an 'upgraded' version of the N7 replica helmet that launched alongside Mass Effect Legendary Edition back in 2020, adding a layer of padding as well as a weathered finish to reflect how the helmet appears in-game.

Two AAA batteries power LED lighting, which can be swapped between Paragon Blue and Renegade Red using an internal switch. No neutral options here.

The helmet is now up for preorder for $174.99, with no indiciation of a release date. Whenever it does ship, that price gets you the wearable helmet as well as a weighted stand, plaque, and challenge coin.

The official Bioware merch drop includes two more 'new' releases: a pair of Converse-like N7 sneakers, and a new T-shirt dedicated to a particularly beloved companion, Garrus Vakarian. Otherwise, the Official Bioware Store has dropped discounts on a range of existing N7 merch, including hats, sweaters, and statues.

The actual products come from DPI Merchandise, a company that has long partnered with Bioware alongside fellow RPG giants like Bethesda and CD Projekt Red.

As for what else fans can expect this weekend? A rumored Mass Effect 5 trailer began circulating around social media platforms soon after news hit of the studio's closure. It's possible Bioware was planning to debut said trailer on N7 Day, but that ship has now sailed.

While a "Save Mess Effect" petition has picked up over 300,000 signatures, for now, fans will have to make do with the merch.

Reports have continued to trickle out about what exactly led to the studio’s closure. Saudi Arabi's PIF, Silver Lake, and Jared Kushner's Affinity Partners completed their acquisition of EA this past August in a deal valued at $55 billion . The company was quick to announce a new strategy focused on "core titles" and increased investment in AI development.

One report suggests EA’s new strategy led the company to a choice between Star Wars: Battlefront 3 and Mass Effect 5, and the company went with the former. A newly announced documentary will hopefully answer questions about what exactly went down in Bioware’s final years, while paying tribute to a studio that defined the modern RPG .

Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

articles.title: Dane Cook and Robert Bowling Announce Vicious Vocab, a Genre-Bending Word Game With a Big Twist
articles.summary: Ex-Call of Duty creative strategist Robert Bowling and comedian Dane Cook have revealed a brand new genre-bending video game known as Vicious Vocab, exclusively to IGN.
articles.body:
Ex- Call of Duty creative strategist Robert Bowling and comedian Dane Cook have revealed a brand new, genre-bending video game known as Vicious Vocab, exclusively to IGN.

Vicious Vocab is a genre-bending spin on casual word games like Scrabble, Words With Friends, and Wordle, with a big twist. While Bowling and Cook are careful not to share much about the twist to preserve some surprises, the game goes well beyond mixing and matching letters to make new words. The words have power and meaning… and they can dramatically change not only what happens to you, but the entire genre of game that you’re playing.

Check out the trailer below to get an idea of the unexpected shift that happens in Vicious Vocab.

Made by a team of five people who collectively call themselves “funcool games,” Vicious Vocab is described as “Scrabble meets Balatro in a backroom casino.” On its own, it’s a fun twist on the word game genre. There’s an action element, which has led the team to referring to the game as a “word brawler” or, in Cook’s words, a first-person speller.

You can “take damage” based on certain words. You can then counter it with another word, so long as you have the right letters. For instance, as seen in the trailer, if you spell out “torch” or “fire,” you might take fire damage. You can then spell out “water” or “ice” and extinguish the flame to stop yourself from taking more damage. These effects add interesting layers to the expected mechanics of a word game.

“That's something you don't get in normal word games,” said Bowling when speaking with IGN. “Building systems that work against systems that work against other systems. When you're four layers deep in a combo, that is the stuff that really makes you feel like, 'Am I playing a word game anymore?' I know I'm making words, I know I'm using letters, but the sort of chaining of events you can get yourself into really sort of that's when you start breaking out of one genre and start making something new.”

However, as the trailer reveals, Vicious Vocab can shift in an incredibly unexpected direction, taking it from a cozy game your mom might play casually on the couch to something in line with The Stanley Parable. If you play the right words, you can move away from the word board and have an entirely new experience that you would've never anticipated.

"We both want to create holy s**t moments," said Cook. "We want to create memorable moments."

Although there are plans to add multiplayer to the game at some point, it is a single-player narrative driven game. If you want to, you can just stick to the more traditional word game and play that “infinitely,” but the game also expands in a whole other direction beyond that.

“We're building out a very deep single player experience that has over 20 different narrative endings, lots of achievements, but the plan is to also expand into a multiplayer experience,” said Bowling. “So there is going to be both. They go in very different directions though, where the multiplayer experience is all about replayability and the single player experience is all about a lot of endings, still a lot of replayability. You can still play it infinitely, but there's a lot more narrative to it that may or may not be in the multiplayer side of it. Think about it as a stem that breaks off into two directions and they get equally weird, but in different ways.”

The pairing of an ex-Call of Duty developer and a comedian is one that may seem unlikely, but it actually dates back 20 years. The two met when Bowling was starting out as a community manager at Infinity Ward and somehow, this led to them playing Call of Duty 2 together. During a match of Capture the Flag, Bowling was impressed that Cook was actually a valuable asset who played the objective instead of mindlessly running around trying to farm kills. From there, a friendship was formed, which eventually led to Cook lending his voice to the “battle chatter” (voice lines for characters yelling out commands and call outs in-game) in the Modern Warfare games.

Over the years, Cook would drum up cool ideas for a game to pitch to Bowling, but it wasn’t until about a year ago when one of those seeds actually began to materialize into a full-fledged game. The initial idea was simple: a word game where your words have an effect. If you write "bomb," it might blow up the other words on the board. It was cute and novel, but as the small team began to brainstorm ideas for effects, it eventually took them into new unexpected directions, such as moving away from the word board.

If this were any other game, developers might say this is a bad idea, because it can lead to a spiral of new mechanics and concepts, but funcool games felt that this exploration that knocks down boundaries and defined genre identities was exciting and worth pursuing.

“It's like, ‘No, I want the game to be wherever it takes us and then see how far can we go,’" said Bowling. “Because you do have some natural constraints from a design standpoint. It's not [like you can] literally do anything because this is all bespoke, handcrafted stuff. So then the question became like, ‘Oh my God, how far can you go with just seven letters and your vocabulary?’ That became the sort of development mantra of, ‘Where is the end?’ And I'll be honest with you, we haven't found it yet. You can get yourself in a lot of weird scenarios with just seven letters, and that has been the most fun. Honestly, when we first started talking about this idea, I loved it as a nugget of the ideal, enough to be like, ‘All right, let's dig into it.’ But I didn't yet know how deep you could go with it.

“Once I cracked that nut creatively, I was like, ‘I love this. I need to play this and I want it to get extremely weird. Dane has a better vocabulary than me. I always go back to weird. I think Stanley Parable. I think give me something where I'm like, ‘What the hell is happening?’"

For Cook, this is sort of a culmination of his career. When he was a kid, his dad would read the dictionary to have a better vocabulary for his job, as he was a color commentator for local hockey games. Cook thought this was “lame” when he was young, but grew to have a better understanding of that process once he became a comic. His entire job as a stand up comic is about using carefully calculated vocabulary to have the best effect on the audience.

“I later found myself saying to him, ‘I paint verbal pictures, and if I repeat the same word over and over, it's blurring the audible version, the audio version, and yet if I have different vernacular for ways to describe something, you're always giving it musicality,’” said Cook. “So lo and behold, I used to have screensavers, word of the day, and things that I could then implement into my standup that I thought helped the musicality paint the verbal pictures.

“I love language, and it's something that to this day when you come down and see me do a show, you'll go, ‘Oh wait, I saw that you used ‘malleable’ to describe blah, blah, blah, blah." I say, "Yeah, because I think it danced better than just saying ‘bent.’ So, [words are] very much a part of my identity and how I like to impact. And again, as a fan of games like this, growing up, playing Scrabble, these are the games that I've always appreciated and enjoyed. So, to feel like I might be able to take it to a new place that also maybe even expands on what those games have been, I hope we pull it off, because I'm really excited at the possibilities.”

In addition to Vicious Vocab, Robert Bowling is also working on a new, larger-scale FPS game from a new studio known as //18.bravo . The game will feature a single-player story and a PvP multiplayer mode, but the game is actively pushing back on live-service trends. Dane Cook also has a new documentary titled Funny Money available on Netflix today.

Vicious Vocab will release on PC at an undisclosed date in the not-too-distant future. No pricing plan has been decided yet.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: Best Buy's Ultimate Holiday Gift Guide for Consoles, Accessories, Games and More
articles.summary: Treat yourself or shop for the gamer in your life and make their holiday the best ever.
articles.body:
The holidays are fast approaching, and that means gift research and deals hunting has already begun. It can be quite a task to narrow down what products are worth buying in the world of gaming and tech right now, even if you’re just prioritizing what to get for yourself. You may be a hardcore gamer looking for upgrades that are worth it, or just getting into gaming and looking for some guidance. On the other hand, you may have landed here seeking ideas of what to give the amer in your life. No matter what it is, this holiday gift guide has something for everyone who games.

In IGN’s gamer gift guide you’ll find top picks across PC, consoles, hardware, accessories and of course, the most fun and anticipated video games of the year. Let’s get into our list to see what and where to get everything you need in one place, all available at Best Buy.

Logitech G PRO X2 SUPERSTRIKE LIGHTSPEED

PlayStation 5 Slim Digital Edition Console– 825GB

Arctis Nova Pro Omni 2.4 GHz Wireless Over-The-Ear Gaming Headset

Let's start with the big gift idea on gamers’ lists: consoles. If you know the person doesn’t already own the latest consoles (maybe they have older generations or handhelds at the moment) then these are no-brainers. Whether the giftee is Team Xbox, Team PlayStation, or ready to go all-in on PC, these are the best console gifts for the 2026 holiday season.

This is the top-of-the-line experience for XBOX fans who want the cream of the crop. If they already have a nice TV or monitor to take advantage of the Series X’s power, this is the version to get versus the Series S below. It includes convenient features such as: Quick Resume, which lets you switch easily between games, backwards compatibility which lets you play four generations of games, and lightning-fast load times, perfect for huge games that require that kind of power. It can easily handle 4K gaming at up to 120FPS, bringing in high resolutions. If the person you’re shopping for has a shelf full of physical games, then this is the one to go with as it has a disc drive and the Series S does not.

If you're looking for an Xbox console that’s smaller and more affordable, the Xbox Series S All Digital console might be the better choice. The Series S has a significantly smaller form factor, doesn't include a disc drive, and targets 1440p resolution instead of 4K. It’s best suited for younger players as a first console, or for someone who isn’t trying to squeeze out every last pixel.

PlayStation 5 Slim Digital Edition Console – (825GB)

For PlayStation fans, we'd recommend getting your hands on the ever-popular PlayStation 5 Slim Digital Edition console (825GB). Like its name suggests, the PlayStation 5 Slim is the PS5 console but shrunk down in size. Jada Griffin's IGN review said: "The slimmed-down PlayStation 5 maintains all of its strengths. Extremely fast loading times and a best-in-class controller make it a pleasure to use." Plus, it’s got tons of storage and a whole backlog of PS4 games (more than 4,000 of them) and new PS5 games available to download from your PS account. It also has the benefits that come with a DualSense® controller, like haptic feedback to immerse yourself in any world you visit. Anyone who loves cinematic, story-driven games would love this console, especially if you have a 4K TV to bring out the new level of realism from your favorite games. Please note this is digital only, so physical games won’t work with this console.

In short, this is a high-performing gaming laptop, especially for the form factor and at this price. If the gamer in your life is just getting into PC gaming, or if they've been looking for something to take with them on the go, this is an easy win. It's got an AMD Ryzen 200 Series R7 260 processor with 8 cores and Zen 4 architecture, 16GB of RAM, and an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5050 card. In other words, this is a perfect gift for students or dual-users, for someone who needs a laptop for work and/or school, but wants to play games at the end of the day. It’s also a good gift for anyone who travels and doesn’t want a handheld PC like a Steam Deck or Lenovo Legion GO.

If you want something powerful for at-home gaming, then this CyberPowerPC is a great option for PC gamers who need a solid setup. This specific version comes with an AMD Ryzen 79800X3D, an AMD Radeon RX 9070 graphics card, 32GB of DDR5 RAM, and 1 terabyte worth of storage. This means it should run games very smoothly for a long period of time, and later on, the PC gamer can decide to upgrade the internals if they want to invest more in their setup. With a desktop PC like this, there are capabilities for streaming or handling games at a higher fidelity, allowing people to upgrade specific components like RAM, CPUs, or graphics cards.

If they need to take it on the go, then a laptop. If they have a desk and want the most power for their at-home setup? Desktop.

Now, for the gamer who already has a PC and a console in their life but still can't get enough immersion, then VR may be an exciting gift for them this year. The Meta Quest 3S is a fully wireless VR headset that can run hundreds of games, including Batman: Arkham Shadow, Beat Saber, and VRChat. And, the Meta Quest 3S is not just for gamers either; it has apps like YouTube and Netflix, allowing users to create a private movie theater in their own living room. It’s an impressive piece of tech that’s all handled on the headset itself, making it easy to get setup and start gaming.

Now that we’ve covered the core gamer basics, it’s time to go over some accessories that can support the gaming experience, whether it be late-night gaming on the couch or at the desk. There are so many accessories that people will wishlist and not end up buying for themselves since they may not feel it’s a “need” to prioritize, but trust us, it’s definitely something they would love to have.

Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike Lightspeed Gaming Mouse

If the person you’re shopping for is on a PC, you want to ensure they have a good gaming mouse. And believe it or not, not all mice are created equal. This Logitech G mouse is hands down the one to beat when it comes to performance. It's super lightweight, comfortable, and most importantly, it’s super fast.

For the PC nerds out there, this mouse has the HERO 2 sensor with a max sensitivity of 44,000 DPI, and HITS tech, which can cut down click latency by up to 30 ms. You can adjust the feel and volume of clicking with 6 intensity levels, allowing you to minimize the sound of clicking as well. If the gamer plays shooting or multiplayer strategy games like MOBAs (Multiplayer Online Battle Arena), or any game where every millisecond counts, then this is THE mouse to get.

When you think of PlayStation peripherals, you usually think of the DualSense® controller or the PULSE 3D headset. But did you know that they also make a gaming monitor? This PlayStation 27" Gaming Monitor is super slick, has an HDR-capable QHD screen, and can handle up to 120 Hertz when connected to a PS5, and up to 240 Hertz on compatible devices. Unlike other monitors, it has a built-in DualSense® controller charging hook, making it a clean setup for their desk. DualSense® wireless controller sold separately.

SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Omni 2.4 GHz Wireless Over-The-Ear Gaming Headset

When it comes to gaming headsets, the Arctis Nova Pro Omni is the best of the best, both in gaming and daily life. The audio quality on these is excellent, and it features hot-swappable batteries for uninterrupted use. The coolest part, though, is the universal base station, which lets you connect to up to three gaming systems at the same time via USB. This headset also features Bluetooth connectivity, so you can connect to your phone and take it on the go to make the most of the Active Noise Cancellation to keep you locked in.

If you're looking for similar performance with a lot of style, check out the Turtle Beach® Stealth Pro II wireless gaming headset. With Hi-Res certified 24-bit/96kHz wireless audio over an ultra low-latency 2.4GHz USB connection, and featuring Dolby Atmos® spatial audio and adjustable active noise cancellation, you'll hear every moment with incredible clarity and detail.

As a little bonus, the FPS Galaxy Black Thumbsticks for XBOX or PlayStation 5 controllers are a great stocking stuffer idea! They make a great add-on to pretty much any gamer’s controller, adding better grip and well, control.

Now for the easy-to-wrap items. We can’t emphasize this enough: Please double-check what platforms your loved ones have before you buy them a game (unless you’re literally the one gifting them the console yourself so you know!) The worst feeling for the gift receiver is getting a physical game for a console they don’t even own, so be sure to double check their preference.

Best for action adventure and Marvel fans

PlayStation fans have been waiting years for Marvel's Wolverine. If you’re shopping for someone who is both a Marvel fan and a gamer, or has played any of the Spider-Man games and liked them, OR likes action games in general and owns (or is about to own) a PS5, this is an excellent game to give them. It should be noted that this game is best suited for adults as it has an M-Rating, so it’s not suitable for the younger folks. Wolverine’s linear level structure, focus on melee combat, and stunning visuals make it a no-brainer game to get. It's got a great cast of X-Men faces and villains, and a stack of accessibility and difficulty options, so it works whether your gamer is a hack-and-slash veteran or just wants to feel like Wolverine.

Marvel’s Wolverine is out now exclusively on PS5, so if you’re going all out on gifts and pairing a game with the PS5 Slim console, this is the perfect game to wrap next to it. © 2026 MARVEL

Not much more needs to be said about GTA VI that hasn’t already been said across the internet, including on IGN.com , but if you’re new here and shopping for a family member or friend, here’s what you need to know.

If the (adult) gamer in your life somehow hasn't pre-ordered GTA VI yet, get it for them now. We can’t stress this enough. GTA VI has been in development for over a decade and is easily the most anticipated game people (like us) won’t stop talking about. It’s THAT crazy of a game and it honestly is more than a game at this point. Even people who haven’t owned GTA before but maybe have played at a friend’s house from time to time will want their hands on this one to not miss out on all the hype (and memes) that will come from this game.

The game isn’t released yet, but it’s available to preorder. It launches November 19th on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S which is right before the holidays. Pair this game with a Series X or a PS5, and you’ll be one of the most legendary gift givers ever. And of course, same note as Wolverine: if the title didn’t give it away, Grand Theft Auto has always been a mature series, so make sure it’s the right fit for whoever you’re shopping for.

Many gamers believe The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is the greatest game of all time, so when the game was rebuilt for Nintendo Switch 2 just in time for Zelda's 40th anniversary, it was a huge deal. It's perfect for the longtime Zelda fan who played the game on N64, or for someone who's all about adventure and exploring in games and is suitable for all ages. It's the same legendary adventure through Hyrule - and through time - rebuilt from the ground up with modern visuals and some smart new touches. You can’t go wrong with this one.

Also See These Must-Have Console-Exclusive Games

From next-gen consoles and gaming PCs to killer headsets and the biggest games of the year, there's something on this list for every kind of gamer. Happy shopping and happy holidays!

articles.title: Xbox Series X | X25 Special Edition Console – Invite Requests Are Up at Amazon
articles.body:
Back in August, when preorders went up for the translucent green Xbox Series X | X25 Special Edition console, they sold out almost instantly. That was a bummer for longtime Xbox fans who wanted to get their hands on one of these limited-edition 25th-anniversary consoles. Now you have another chance, thanks to Amazon. Instead of doing preorders on a first-come-first-served basis, Amazon is letting anyone interested request an invite to buy this special-edition Xbox (you can request one here ).

Xbox Series X - X25 Limited Edition Invite Request

Requesting an invite doesn’t mean you’ll necessarily end up being invited to buy a console. But it gives you a chance to be invited, which is better than nothing. As Amazon says, “If invited to purchase, you’ll get an email when the item is available. Not all requests will be granted.”

The console is meant to celebrate the 25th anniversary of Xbox. It’s set to release on November 13 and costs (the curiously specific price) $909.23. Only 25,000 numbered consoles are being manufactured, which explains the difficulty people have had securing a preorder.

So what do you get if you do end up buying it? You get a 1TB Xbox Series X console, decked out in translucent green. The front of the console has an X25 logo, and when you turn it on, the X logo glows green as well. You also get a matching controller (which is also sold separately, and is still available at some retailers). Finally, you get a digital copy of Halo: Campaign Evolved, a remake of the campaign from the original Halo (see our review ).

XBOX Wireless Controller X25 Special Edition (Available Now)

XBOX Wireless Controller X25 Special Edition

Overall, this has been an extremely popular item among IGN readers. It’s a great-looking piece of hardware that celebrates 25 years since the original Xbox hit store shelves. If you want one, or even if you might be interested in one, there’s no reason not to request an invite.

articles.title: Canadian Politician Petitions Government to Help BioWare Buy Its Way From Under EA
articles.summary: A Canadian politician has started an official government petition to save Mass Effect developer BioWare.
articles.body:
Update: Canadian MP Don Davies has provided comment on the BioWare petition:

“BioWare has cultivated an international following from their renowned video game franchises like Mass Effect, Baldur’s Gate, and Dragon Age. Canada’s video game industry creates some of our most important cultural exports, and BioWare was among our biggest success stories.

Electronic Arts, their American parent company, was never invested in the success of BioWare since they purchased the studio as part of a larger acquisition in 2007. This is a pattern with video game publishers like EA. They buy smaller developers, set unrealistic timelines, overwork their employees, and meddle in the development process, resulting in poorer quality games. Then, when sales fail to meet expectations, they blame the developers, lay off workers, and eventually shut down the studio for short-term profit.

New Democrats want BioWare to stay in business, preferably under Canadian control. We believe that the employees at BioWare ought to have the first opportunity to buy back their studio and continue making the games that fans love. The petition primarily asks the federal government to provide the required capital. This is absolutely possible. Our goal with the petition is to demonstrate just how many Canadians believe this is a worthwhile investment in our entertainment industry.”

It's already been a couple of weeks since EA shut down BioWare , but the fight to save the studio is still picking up steam. And now, after a fanmade petition reached 300,000 signatures , a Canadian politician has started an official government petition to save the Mass Effect developer.

Petition e-7898 was initiated by Burnaby, British Columbia resident Brendan Routh, and sponsored by Vancouver Kingsway MP Don Davies. The petition primarily calls upon the Canadian government to provide BioWare with the necessary capital to secure independence and ownership of its intellectual property. However, it further asks the government to protect Canadian businesses from "being dictated by American and foreign corporate interests."

The petition also asks the government to "champion the values of inclusivity, tolerance, democracy, justice, and civil rights at the centre of Canada's national identity by preserving BioWare's invaluable contribution to the global entertainment industry."

At the time of writing, the petition has already racked up 2,861 signatures. And while that's a far cry from the 307,000 signatures on the change.org petition, the Canadian government only requires that 500 people sign it before it's brought before the House of Commons for discussion. And while it will be presented to the House of Commons, it remains to be seen whether or not the Canadian government will actually act on it.

However, Don Davies has taken to Bluesky to argue the petition's merits. In a post, Davies argues "BioWare’s US parent company, EA, has decided to close the studio. These publishers buy developers, run them into the ground, and rip them apart for profit. There's a pattern of US companies buying Canadian businesses and shutting them down, costing Canadians their jobs."

In a followup post, Davies continues: "The developers at BioWare know how to run their studio. They know how to make the games that fans love. They should be given the first opportunity – and the federal support – to buy it and run it themselves."

This petition comes a little over a week after another Canadian politician, Avi Lewis, spoke out about the closure, and floated the idea of the Canadian government helping BioWare gain its independence from EA. But, now that there's a petition that has crossed its signature threshold, there's actually a slim possibility that something is going to happen.

I've reached out to Don Davies for comment, and I'll update this article if I hear anything. But, who knows; maybe there's a chance that something will come of that incredible leaked Mass Effect 5 trailer, after all.

articles.title: God of War Ragnarok Tops List of 10 Highest-Grossing PlayStation Studios Games From the PS5 Generation

articles.body:
Sony Santa Monica Studios' God of War Ragnarok tops the list of highest-grossing PlayStation Studios games of the PS5 generation, according to Alinea Analytics.

The game data company's head of market analysis, Rhys Elliott, shared information related to sales for titles published under the PlayStation banner in a Substack post today. It features a list of 10 games estimated to have emerged as Sony's best performers so far.

You can probably guess at least some of the games that managed to crack the top 10 list, but there are a few interesting inclusions in there, too. God of War Ragnarok, for example, is placed at number one with an estimated $1.4 billion in gross revenue. Spider-Man 2 is second at $1.3 billion, with Gran Turismo 7 placed third at $841.9 million. You can see the full list below.

Together, the 10 games generated over $6.5 billion across PlayStation (84.7%), Steam (14.1%), and Xbox (1.2% via just Helldivers 2). Full write-up over on Substack. — Rhys Elliott (@superhys) November 6, 2026

Here's the 10 top-grossing PlayStation Studios games of this generation (@alineaanalytics estimates). Together, the 10 games generated over $6.5 billion across PlayStation (84.7%), Steam (14.1%), and Xbox (1.2% via just Helldivers 2). Full write-up over on Substack.

PlayStation Studios' Top 10 Highest-Grossing PS5 Games, According to Alinea Analytics

5. Horizon Forbidden West – $485.8 million

7. The Last of Us Part 1 – $341.3 million

8. Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart – $334.9 million

These 10 games alone have generated $6.5 billion for PlayStation. Although the list only includes titles from the PS5 generation, the numbers here do account for other platforms. Astro Bot, for example, is exclusive to PS5 and earned its amount only through the estimated 4.7 million copies it sold on that platform.

God of War Ragnarok, meanwhile, is also available on PS4 and PC, with Alinea Analytics' breakdown showing its revenue accumulated via 21.6 million copies across all three platforms. Of its performance on PlayStation, 75.2% of its 20.1 million share of copies sold were on PS5, specifically, with 27.5% of all sales on PS4 and PS5 being physical. Elliott called the Norse God of War sequel an evergreen title for Sony, explaining that in 2026 alone it's managed to sell 1.1 million copies. That's an impressive feat compared even to brand-new games from this year, and it's only more impressive when you consider that it was made accessible to PlayStation Extra subscribers nearly two years ago in January of 2025. Alinea Analytics estimates show that 6.7 million PlayStation Plus users have accessed it via the service.

articles.title: GTA 6 Players in Germany Can Legally Take Time Off Work to Play the Game on Launch, But There's a Catch
articles.summary: Germany has a unique legal loophole that lets 60 employees take time off work to play GTA 6 without putting their jobs in jeopardy.
articles.body:
Germany has a unique legal loophole that lets 60 employees take time off work to play GTA 6 without putting their jobs in jeopardy.

GTA 6 is shaping up to be one of the biggest pop culture moments in history, and perhaps the biggest video game launch of all time. With this in mind, it’s no surprise that oodles of gamers are planning to call out of work to play it, with estimates showing a 17% increase in time-off requests for its launch date on November 19.

This trend isn’t limited to the US, either, as a fair amount of fans across the globe will also be staying home to play. Luckily, fans in Germany literally have legal protections that will allow them to do this without putting their jobs on the line.

Bildungsurlaub, Germany's legally mandated paid learning leave for certified training courses, is offering a state-funded educational course on storytelling in video games that would give gamers three days off to play GTA 6 from November 18 - 20. Titled ‘Open World Games: Lessons from a Digital World,’ this program is open to 60 participants, letting them use this paid leave to “explore storytelling, digital culture, and collaboration through open-world gaming,” as explained in a press release shared with IGN.

Students will gather in guided groups to complete assignments in the game and use their observations to learn “practical lessons on storytelling, motivation, community-building, and collaboration.” One of these lessons explores how Easter eggs create engagement with players, examining how brands, learning programs, and teams can “borrow from that dynamic.”

“Modern learning should meet people where their curiosity already lives. Open worlds are built on stories, choices, communities, and constant problem-solving. That makes them powerful places to learn,” says Carlo Dreschel, founder of course provider Dein Bildungsurlaub . “Like many other educational providers, we've incorporated elements of gaming, such as role-playing, simulations, game mechanics and reward systems, into learning experiences before. But with ‘Open World Games,’ we're taking that approach to an entirely new level.”

23-year-old accountant Victoria is one of the students who’s signed up for this course. Hailing from Berlin, she’s an “avid gamer” who says she’s curious about how this program will aid her professional life.

“I am curious to see what I can really learn from the experience. My usual day to day is driven by routine. I believe the course will break this routine and offer a new perspective to the same old problems. Maybe the experience of pulling off a high speed car chase can help me handle stressful clients in the future,” she said in a statement.

Participants must be 18 years of age or older and have access to a suitable device and a licensed open-world game in order to take part in this course. It will take place over a three-day period online, with an additional in-person event planned in Berlin.

Germany isn't the only country getting ahead of the GTA 6 employment crater; Australia's workplace regulator put out a helpful graphic informing workers of their paid leave rights ahead of the game's launch. And in July, a flyer from the 9th Engineer Battalion in Fort Stewart, Georgia went viral for offering recruits a four-day pass to play GTA 6 with a “special reenlistment incentive."

We at IGN even polled our readers to see how many of you are planning to take time off work to play the game, and the results were surprisingly split down the middle. GTA 6 launches November 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox X/S.

articles.title: This Disturbing Horror Movie Is Free on Tubi Right Now - I Don’t Know if You Should Watch It
articles.body:
Some horror films make you scream, some make you question if human intestines really stretch that far, and some are named after a piece of furniture and leave psychological scarring. The Coffee Table's title and thumbnail aren't going to stand out when you're scrolling through the Tubi movie library, but take a chance on it and you'll experience a story that starts with one seemingly banal decision and turns it into an extended nightmare on a par with Martyrs and the original Danish version of Speak No Evil.

The Coffee Table is free to watch on Tubi now and starts like a domestic drama. Jesus and Maria are an unhappy couple with a new baby, shopping for furniture with resentment hanging over them like a poisonous fog. Jesus takes a shine to a mid-century meets brothel aesthetic monstrosity made of glass and metal, and when his wife says she doesn't want it, the argument quickly spirals from interior design to a battleground for Jesus's insecurity about the lack of power he has in the relationship, in everything from the color of their home's walls to the timing of their first child. He insists on taking the table home, and the consequences of that decision are so much worse than just a marital counselling session.

The spoiler-free version is this: he gets it home, and Maria leaves to buy food and wine ahead of an impending family visit that afternoon. The baby is crying, assembling the table is made more difficult by a missing screw, and then, almost out of nowhere, the big, terrible, awful thing happens. The movie suddenly becomes a death drop towards an inevitable end, and however much you want to look away, you can't help but keep watching. The action never strays far beyond the confines of Jesus and Maria's apartment, but the tension keeps building. It's not so much nail-biting as stomach-ulcer-inducing. Like some of the best horror movies, I can tell you that it's sharply written, brutally delivered, and truly ghastly, but at the same time, I want to sit down with anyone about to watch it and check that they wouldn't want to go for something gentler like, say, The Substance or Obsession instead.

Mega, upsetting spoilers beyond this point

Still with me because you can't wait to or don't want to watch it, but your twisted curiosity has gotten the better of you? Then buckle up. To put it gently, the table becomes the site of what we can call a Hereditary moment for Jesus and Maria's son. Utterly paralyzed with shock, Jesus attempts to continue as if nothing has happened, placing the baby's headless body in its crib and cleaning up the blood. Maria returns home, but Jesus manages to keep her away from their son, but as the audience we know that, like some sort of beheaded Chekhov’s gun, the horrible truth will be uncovered before the movie ends. From there, director Caye Casas just piles on the pressure with family arriving, a neighbor girl who falsely accuses Jesus of inappropriate behavior, a family pregnancy announcement that Jesus doesn't greet with joy, and a pet dog that goes a little bit too Sherlock Holmes and finds the aforementioned missing head under a chair. Needless to say, it's not a happy ending, and any relief the audience might be feeling that the nightmare is over just never seems to come. There's no closure or sense of justice – just one terrible thing that happened.

Boiled down to that pretty basic A to B, the movie could sound like just a cheap shock, but the bloody reality of the situation is restrained so that your discomfort comes instead from your imagination and because of the utter senseless, accidental nature of Jesus's situation. The film is just 90 minutes long, but it will stay with you long after the credits have rolled.

articles.title: Ed Boon Wants to Know What Fans Want the Next Mortal Kombat Game to Be Called
articles.summary: Ed Boon is stirring up excitement in the fighting game community after releasing a poll asking fans what they’d like the next Mortal Kombat installment to be called.
articles.body:
Ed Boon is stirring up excitement in the fighting game community after releasing a poll asking fans what they’d like the next Mortal Kombat installment to be called.

It’s been a rough time for Mortal Kombat fans. The series’ latest game, MK1, officially stopped receiving new content updates in May 2025, and its presence at competitive tournaments has been lackluster, at best.

Players are eager for more news on the next game in the franchise, which co-creator Ed Boon confirmed was officially in the works in May 2026. It’s been pretty quiet since then — but now, it appears that Boon is testing the waters to see what fans are expecting.

Mortal Kombat Flawless Victory: A Visual History of the Iconic Series Excerpt

On November 6, 2026, Boon published two polls on X/Twitter. The first asked, “What would you want the next Mortal Kombat to be called?” giving options for Mortal Kombat 13, Mortal Kombat 12, and Mortal Kombat 2. (Thus far, 43% of participants have voted for Mortal Kombat 2, with 33% choosing 13 and 23% choosing 12.)

His second poll is far more intriguing, asking: “With two great Marvel fighting games being made by different teams, which would you like to see come out next? Marvel Tokon 2 by Arc System Works, or Marvel vs Capcom 4?” (Unsurprisingly, the overwhelming majority of fans chose MvC4.)

With 2 great Marvel fighting games being made by different teams. Which would you like to see come out next? Marvel Tokkon 2 by Arc System works. or Marvel vs Capcom 4 — Ed Boon (@noobde) November 6, 2026

With 2 great Marvel fighting games being made by different teams. Which would you like to see come out next? Marvel Tokkon 2 by Arc System works. or Marvel vs Capcom 4

This is an interesting query coming from the developer of the Injustice series, and an odd one, given that the likelihood of another Marvel vs Capcom game happening anytime soon — if ever — seems extremely improbable. The FGC has already tied itself in knots about Tokon’s player count and difficult PC launch , while, mechanically, there’s a significant divide as to whether or not it’s actually fun at a competitive level. On the other hand, the MvC series appeared to die a slow, painful death with Infinite , though it has received a second wind over the last few years (in no small part thanks to the Beyond fan mod ).

This question follows oodles of rumors regarding the next Injustice game, which has been all but outright confirmed by Boon. Fans have already uncovered resumes from stunt performers that list Injustice 3, and rumors that playtests were underway for the game surfaced earlier this year.

Boon reacted to the rumors back in September in response to a tweet claiming that NetherRealm was testing Injustice 3, Mortal Kombat 13, and / or Mortal Kombat 9. “All false,” he wrote. “Appreciate the interest & enthusiasm, but just because a game isn’t currently being tested externally doesn’t necessarily mean the game isn’t in development.”

For now, we’ll just have to wait and see what Boon and NetherRealm have in store for their next game. In the meantime, you can read our interview with the cast of the Street Fighter movie , who said they’re more than willing to take part in a crossover film with the cast of the Mortal Kombat franchise. Boon even responded to our report , saying that he’d rather have a Street Fighter x Mortal Kombat game before a movie gets made.

articles.title: ‘I Meant It When I Said What I Said’ — Nicolas Cage is Actually Relieved That Spider-Noir Got Canceled
articles.summary: IGN got the chance to catch up with Nicolas Cage on the red carpet for his upcoming sports comedy flick Madden, where he opened up about his thoughts on Spider-Noir’s cancellation.
articles.body:
IGN got the chance to catch up with Nicolas Cage on the red carpet for his upcoming sports comedy flick Madden, where he opened up about his thoughts on Spider-Noir’s cancellation.

Released on Prime Video earlier this year, Cage stars as Ben Reilly in this animated take on New York’s resident web-slinger. Available to watch in both black and white and color, the show received strong reviews on the outset, but officially got canned by the streamer in September after falling out of its top 10 shows — oddly, much to Cage’s relief.

In a statement to Deadline, Cage said, “For me, one season is perfect, having said what I wanted to say with this dangerous, innovative, pop-art Spider-Man. Onwards, upwards, inwards.”

Spider-Noir #1 Exclusive Preview Gallery

He doubled down on this sentiment while chatting with IGN’s Jeffrey Vega in early November, who asked if the actor felt there was still more of Ben Reilly’s story left to tell.

“No,” Cage answered. “I meant it when I said what I said. It’s a perfect season. You never wanna get stuck repeating a character and wear out your welcome. Ben Riley is so idiosyncratic. I was doing something that was pretty high-risk, tightrope stuff — if you do that for season 2, season 3, you could really wear out your welcome.

“So when they didn’t pick it up, I was like, 'Whew, thank you!' Because now I’m doing True Detective, and that’s only one season. It’s better that way, you know? I liked it when you would see Rock Hudson and Macmillan ? and it’s one season. I didn’t wanna keep repeating it. I don’t like repeating myself. It’s perfect, and I love that character. I love that season, and it will always be there and always be fresh.”

Aside from not wanting to rehash his character’s story, Cage wouldn’t return to the Spider-Noir series anyway, as he famously parted ways with Amazon over its stance on AI. In a blistering statement , he revealed that he refused to sign a waiver to use artificial intelligence on the animated series and confirmed that he was unlikely to ever work with the company again.

"Amazon is a very AI-friendly company, to the tune of $50 billion invested in OpenAI. I'm not an AI-friendly actor," Cage said. "I'm not part of their club. I didn't sign the waiver to use AI on Spider-Noir. I'll probably not work with that studio again, but that's OK."

Cage has been open about his distaste for AI, saying at the 2025 Saturn Awards that "Robots cannot reflect the human condition for us. That is a dead end if an actor lets one AI robot manipulate his or her performance even a little bit, an inch will eventually become a mile and all integrity, purity, and truth of art will be replaced by financial interests only. We can’t let that happen."

Cage is currently gearing up for the November 18 release of Madden , wherein he portrays the titular John Madden – a performance that has already been a source of viral debate among fans.
