Warning! Spoilers ahead for Godzilla Minus Zero .

Godzilla Minus Zero has the most viscerally violent kaiju battle since Gareth Edwards’ 2014 Godzilla . I’d say it easily surpasses that , even with Godzilla’s atomic-heat-ray-down-the-throat finishing move against the bug-like MUTO in Edwards’ movie that rebooted Toho’s franchise after 10 dormant years. In Godzilla Minus Zero, the inevitable showdown between Godzilla and the terrifying three-headed King Ghidorah is a bloody no-holds-barred melee from the get-go, with the two immediately going for each others’ jugular (or whatever the equivalent anatomy is of unknowable monsters from the sea and space). It’s not outlandish to call their fight the most intense monster-on-monster violence portrayed in the franchise’s history. Like Ken Watanabe’s character says in Edwards’ Godzilla, “Let them fight.”

How did writer/director Takashi Yamazaki think about staging this huge, all-out, flesh-ripping, head chopping, arm-tearing kaiju brawl?

“So, I have two cats,” Yamazaki told IGN. “And for the most part, they're very nice and playful with each other, but on a rare occasion I think there's like — I don't know if they're crossing the line between play and actual fighting. I see two creatures fighting each other and I tend to think about my cats when that happens.”

Incredible. Anyone with multiple cats knows exactly what Yamazaki is talking about, and the inspiration is hard to unsee. Ghidorah, even from his first scene of destruction, comes off as somewhat cat-like as he peeks at fleeing people in between buildings, like a cat hunting, before razing the city with his terrifying zaps of thunder breath. Then when he’s done, he goes and curls up to take a long nap in a kaiju-sized bed, also known as a mountain crater.

Like so many of the devastating human elements of Godzilla Minus Zero, the battle scene between Godzilla and Ghidorah takes full advantage of its R rating, the first for a Godzilla film. (Another first: It’s the first time a Japanese film was shot for IMAX.) Making the climax as gory and exciting as it is started all the way back at the script phrase.

“When writing the screenplay for Godzilla Minus Zero, I remember writing, ‘This is a fight to the death.’ There was a duel between two of them and a fight to the death means one will inevitably die,” Yamazaki said. “Thinking about these two beasts that are equipped with the ability to kill each other and if they really go at it, what will happen? Even in nature, you start ripping parts of flesh off and then start to weaken your opponent to the point where you can deliver the finishing blow. So it felt natural that kaiju would also behave similarly in a fight to the death.

“Thinking about this idea that one will inevitably die, I think it's impossible not to think about the sort of chaos that would ensue. But at the same time, I think it's sort of painful and sad to watch because I look at Godzilla and it almost feels like a cat being bullied in a way. And I think since having two cats and watching them so often, I've had this sickness where anything fighting looks like two cats fighting to me.”

Godzilla Minus Zero opens in U.S. theaters on November 6. We liked its "satisfying and visually amazing scenes of giant-monster destruction" in our review . For more Godzilla, read about how Yamazaki told us that focusing on trying to one-up the Oscar-winning Godzilla Minus One in this sequel was a surefire way to “risk diluting what makes the movie great in the first place.” The writer/director is still on the fence about turning his Godzilla movies into a trilogy.

Leanne Butkovic (she/they) is an Editorial Programming Manager at IGN, where they've also written about TV, movies, and games.

articles.title: Pokémon TCG: 10 Most Valuable Delta Reign Cards From New Expansion
articles.summary: Mega Rayquaza ex leads the secondary market surge in the newest Pokémon TCG expansion. Here are the 10 most expensive Delta Reign cards on TCGplayer and eBay.
articles.body:
The Pokémon Company International has officially unleashed Delta Reign - the all-new Pokémon Trading Card Game expansion that finally brings Mega Rayquaza back to tabletop prominence after a long five-year absence since its iconic run in Evolving Skies.

That Rayquaza VMAX (Alternate Art Secret) from Evolving Skies chase card is still one of the most iconic cards of all time , currently sitting at a high of $1,044.19 on TCGplayer .

As collectors race to collect all 141 cards and chase the set's heaviest hitters, the secondary market is already experiencing severe turbulence.

To help you navigate the chaos of Delta Reign’s soaring valuations , we’ve broken down the 10 most expensive cards you can pull in the Delta Reign expansion, according to third-party market TCGPlayer.

This vaguely suggestive card of a Kecleon sliding down a pole, illustrated by Tomokazu Komiya, has proven to be a bit divisive; not everyone is a fan.

I, personally, love the Art Brut-esque art style - it reminds me of colored pencils and crayons, when I would draw all my beloved Hoenn team as a child playing through Pokémon Emerald.

This card can be yours for $16.93, falling from an initial launch price of $25.17. This is a great budget option, and one of my favourites in Delta Reign.

Illustrated by Yoshimoto Yoshimon, who you might know for heavy-hitters like Marill and Slurpuff from Ascended Heroes, this sweet Growlithe card got the ultimate cozy treatment in this adorable new Illustration Rare.

Sat chilling in a pink, sunlit living room, you can almost imagine Growlithe basking in the sun, soaking in those final rays of the day.

With a semi-translucent outline around this original 151 fire pup, it almost looks like a sticker. You can pick this up on release day for $17.67 from TCGPlayer - the price is already falling from a high of $18.92.

This dynamic, colorful card from 5ban Graphics is coming in at number 8 on the most expensive cards of Delta Reign so far. The market average price is sat at $22.12, falling from an initial $23.24.

This awesome Illustration Rare from Ryota Murayama shows off the continent Pokémon in all its glory. It packs a competitive punch too, dealing an extra 170 damage if a Stadium card with "Legendary" in its name is active.

If its current market average of $28.43 is a little too steep for your liking, or if you just played Pokémon Sapphire as a kid, Kyogre is only $0.44 despite being a similarly gorgeous card.

If there’s one thing you should know about me, it’s that I’m a big Eevee fan . So much so that I have over 200 Eeevee plushies in my bedroom. Yes, it’s becoming a bit of a problem.

I adore this card from Hideki Ishikawa, showing Eevee in an adorable picnic scene for $30.37. If I lived in the world of Pokémon, I like to think this card is a snapshot of what my life would look like.

This card from 5ban Graphics has shot up in price since launch - it launched at $23.24, and now sits at $43.99. It’s no surprise really, when you consider the popularity of Mega Evolutions and their relative newness to the TCG.

If you’re a big Mega Golurk fan, you should consider picking this card up sooner rather than later - I wouldn’t be surprised if it starts to spike again.

The Zinnia's Trust Special Illustration Rare, illustrated by GIDORA, just misses out on the top 3 spot. As the devoted Lorekeeper of the Draconid people, Zinnia’s connection to the Draconid legends and her efforts to summon Rayquaza to intercept the Grand Meteor Delta in Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire make her presence in an expansion anchored by Mega Rayquaza feel completely earned. You can pick this card up for $49.49.

Taking the bronze Ribbon for the most expensive card in Delta Reign is this incredible Raikou Special Illustration Rare from aky CG Works. Raikou leaps through a jagged, towering canyon landscape that can’t help but remind me of Mt Thunder from Pokémon Mystery Dungeon Red/Blue games.

A hefty jump into second place here, and it’s no surprise which Mon takes home the silver Ribbons. This Mega Rayquaza ex Special Illustration Rare, illustrated by Kozuki Minami – the same artist that won the 2024 Pokémon TCG Illustration contest thanks to her inspired take on Pikachu, is currently sat at a market average of $334.82.

A fitting card to take home the Gold Ribbon, the Mega Ultra Rare Mega Rayquaza ex, illustrated by takuyoa, is, unsurpsingly perhaps, currently the most expensive card you can find in Delta Reign. TCGPlayer has one currently sold for $349.34, but the average price on eBay is sitting at an eye-watering $500. There are three total Rayquaza cards in this set if you’re looking to hunt them down - the 084/103 Double Rare, and the two mentioned in this list.

There are some gorgeous cards in Delta Reign, and if you’re looking to hunt them down, your best bet is to hunt for Booster Boxes or ETBs at your local game store or online, as they offer the most consistent pull rates for the price. If you want a card in particular, I’d recommend waiting until the market settles so you can get the best value for money. Which card you you hoping to add to your binder? I'll definitely be keepng an eye out for the Eevee card as I mentioned. I also love the Kyogre card, and for that price, you can't really go wrong. There are some really nice cards in this set , and it's shaking out as one of the more affordable ones of recent memory.

articles.title: Avery the Poké Kid's Father Pleads With The Pokémon Company to Make a Trading Card in Honor of His Late Son
articles.summary: The father of late Pokémon influencer Avery the Poké Kid is asking The Pokémon Company to create a special card in honor of his son.
articles.body:
The father of late Pokémon influencer Avery the Poké Kid is asking The Pokémon Company to create a special card in honor of his son.

Avery the Poké Kid was a prominent and cheerful voice in the Pokémon Trading Card Game community. He died in September 2026 at 12 years old in after a seven-year-battle with pancreatic cancer; he went viral posthumously when his family shared a video of his final card pack opening a few days after his death, in which he excitedly pulled a 30th Anniversary Jirachi SIR card.

Now, his father is putting forth a public request to The Pokémon Company to make a special card in Avery’s honor.

On November 6, Christian Garcia — Avery’s father — published a tearful video on Instagram with a special plea to "immortalize" his son in the hobby he loved the most.

“Trying to figure out how to carry on Avery’s legacy has been the biggest challenge of the last couple months,” Garcia said. “…I want to make a plea to anyone, literally anyone from The Pokémon Company: If you’re watching this video, I want to figure out how to immortalize him somehow in the trading card game he loved so much.

“That kid literally was the embodiment of a Pokémon Master, and we’re hopeful, and I think it would be the coolest thing to open up a pack of cards and chase our son. If someone at The Pokémon Company is watching, please get a hold of us.”

Fans and fellow collectors are doing everything they can to get the attention of The Pokémon Company, with most agreeing that it would only make sense to make his card some iteration of a Jirachi, given his viral pull that took over social media after his death.

Avery’s heartbreaking Jirachi pull even caught the attention of the card’s artist, who posted an emotional reaction to the news on her Twitter/X account. “I’m so deeply moved. I’m so glad I kept drawing. I’ve honestly been in tears ever since I saw this,” she wrote. “‘I want my art to bring happiness to people.’ That’s one of the reasons I draw. I’m so glad I put that wish into this piece.”

This latest statement from Avery’s father follows a September announcement from the influencer’s family in response to scalpers inflating the price of the 30th Anniversary Jirachi SIR card as a result of his viral video.

“We are not involved in or benefiting from any cards being sold in Avery’s name or likeness. We have not approved these sales. We have asked sellers to take their listings down. Please do so immediately. This does not honor Avery’s generous heart. We are mourning our son and caring for our children. Please let us do that in peace,” they wrote at the time.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

articles.title: Godzilla Minus Zero Ending Explained and Our Biggest Burning Questions
articles.summary: We've got some questions about Godzilla Minus Zero, as well as how it might set up a third installment in the series.
articles.body:
You want to know if Godzilla Minus Zero has any post-credits scenes, don't you? We'll tell you right here: It does not. Though there is a short audio surprise for those who stick around to the end.

It’s time to go go Godzilla , because Godzilla Minus Zero is now in theaters. The sequel to 2023’s instant classic Godzilla Minus One, Minus Zero reunites director Takashi Yamazaki and his cast for a new adventure featuring the Big G. The film is entering its opening weekend with strong reviews , including a 7/10 from IGN’s Scott Collura, who wrote that it “doesn’t disappoint in the slightest on the kaiju front.” Still, now that we’ve seen the film, we have some questions about certain plot elements and a potential third installment in the series. Let’s get into all the spoilery details of Godzilla Minus Zero.

We have a lot to get through, so we’ll keep the recap part brief. As indicated by the marketing, Ryunosuke Kamiki and Minami Hamabe return as Kōichi and Noriko Shikishima (they got married between films), who rejoin the civilian effort to protect postwar Japan from giant monsters, aka kaiju, while raising their adopted daughter Akiko (Sae Nagatani). It’s now 1949 and the kaiju in question is King Ghidorah, an alien dragon who crashes on Earth inside a meteorite, and the plan is to use Noriko, who’s been infused with Godzilla cells from her encounter with the big guy in the last film, as bait to lure Godzilla into a fight with Ghidorah. While the ensuing battle (seemingly?) kills Ghidorah, it results in the death of Dr. Kenji Noda (Hidetaka Yoshioka), one of Kōichi’s allies from the first film, and also renders the Shikishima family fugitives from the occupying US military, who want to use Noriko’s Godzilla-summoning abilities as a weapon.

There’s more to the movie’s story, such as meteorologist Makoto Aoyama (Masami Nagasawa), who uses her weather predicting powers to help the good guys (more useful than you might think), and Min Tanaka as Professor Murakami, an elderly biologist who builds the device Noriko uses to attract Godzilla’s attention. We’ll talk more about them in a bit. Overall, Minus Zero is a satisfying blockbuster for its kaiju action and endearing characters, and looks incredible on an IMAX screen. However, it’s not as tidy as the previous film, with a few things that left us scratching our heads once the credits started rolling. Namely…

Let it not be said that Godzilla Minus Zero is lacking in spectacle, because the final showdown between Godzilla and King Ghidorah is one for the ages. However, the resolution is a bit strange because we’re not sure what happened to Ghidorah. The battle ends with the two monsters firing their energy beams at each other, and Godzilla’s seems to overpower his foe’s. But we don’t actually see Ghidorah’s fate. The edit here is weird, with Ghidorah just kind of disappearing between cuts; we don’t see a body, nor does he seem to explode into bits. So what happened? We know Ghidorah has incredible regenerative abilities, with him even being infected with Godzilla cells in the final fight (he starts growing Godzilla style dorsal fins while using his beam). Could Ghidorah have survived to menace the world anew? Or did Godzilla’s archenemy actually perish? It’s not quite clear, so we’d like to know!

Why Did Professor Murakami Give Up on His Revenge?

Professor Murakami is a new character in Godzilla Minus Zero, and one of the first people to witness and survive Ghidorah’s wrath. A biologist by trade, Murakami has cell samples of both Godzilla and Ghidorah, and also developed a machine that broadcasts a creature’s “resonance frequency” to draw more members of the same species to its location. Hooking Noriko up to the machine is what lets the heroes lure Godzilla to Ghidorah for the final battle. But Murakami has another use of the device: to get revenge for the death of his family in the bombing of Hiroshima. Halfway through the film, Murakami fantasizes about summoning Godzilla to New York City, where he annihilates Manhattan with an atomic blast. It’s an incredible scene, and paints what could be a fascinating direction for the movie to go… except it doesn’t.

Murakami decides against revenge during the finale, and while Dr. Noda does go to him the night before and pleads for Murakami to give up on his vengeful crusade – Noda insists that “ending the cycle” of violence would be the true way to avenge his family – was that really enough to convince him? It feels like there’s a beat or two missing, some additional motivation for Murakami to change his path and destroy the device after Ghidorah’s defeat. The movie ends with Murakami as a prisoner of the US military, and he says there are “more minds to change.” Perhaps Murakami’s story will continue and we’ll get more light on his mindset if there’s a sequel.

This might seem like an odd question, but walk with me here. Makoto Aoyuma is a meteorologist who joins Dr. Noda’s Disaster Response Bureau, and her weather prediction abilities are surprisingly helpful in developing plans to counteract Ghidorah. She’s the one who suggests using lightning rods dropped from a bomber plane to strike Ghidorah down, and also uses storm patterns to track his movements so the Shikishimas can lure Godzilla to the right spot. That said, this is the 1940s, where weather prediction was much harder to do than it is now due to the limits of the era’s technology. There was even another movie this year, Pressure, a WWII drama about the meteorologists who helped plan the Normandy invasion, which showed how challenging forecasting the weather was at that time (it’s also a pretty good movie if you’re curious). But Aoyuma has an uncanny knack for it.

The only time where she claims she’s failed with weather prediction in the past wasn’t even her fault. She got the forecast right, but people above her didn’t listen. There are even multiple scenes where Aoyuma sticks her head out into the air and seems to “sense” incoming weather like she’s a Jedi using the Force. So is Aoyuma just incredibly gifted in this field, or does she have some supernatural talent? The movie doesn’t say, but since there are psychics and fairies in other Godzilla movies, it wouldn’t be unprecedented.

Was Ghidorah’s Arrival on Earth a Coincidence?

To go back to other precedents in the Godzilla series, although the Minus films are more “realistic” than other interpretations, King Ghidorah is once again an alien in Godzilla Minus Zero. The perennial Godzilla nemesis is usually (but not always) from outer space and often works on behalf of invaders intent on conquering the world. While Ghidorah rides in on a meteorite, there’s no evidence in Minus Zero that it was purposefully sent to Earth by anyone. An invasion by Xiliens may be too pulpy for the tone of Yamazaki’s films, but Ghidorah just showing up only a couple of years after Godzilla and also just so happening to crash-land specifically in Japan is a remarkable set of circumstances. Is there more to Ghidorah’s arrival that we don’t yet know? Maybe this will be explored in another film if Ghidorah did indeed survive.

Why Was Noriko the Only Survivor of Godzilla Cell Infection?

As revealed at the end of Godzilla Minus One, Noriko was infected with Godzilla cells, which gave her enough regenerative ability to survive her injuries in that film. The infection expresses itself in Minus Zero as a discoloration of one eye and a patch of spikes on her right shoulder, which Noriko covers with an eye patch and bandage respectively. We later learn that Noriko was one of a handful of people infected with Godzilla cells, which initially results in a healing factor but then develops into mass mutations which can kill the host. In fact, Noriko is apparently the only person left with Godzilla cells who’s been able to survive long-term. So what makes Noriko so special? Is it just an unknown quirk of biology, or is there a greater explanation that Professor Murakami didn’t have time to study? Since Noriko is the only person who can power the “summon Godzilla” machine, we’d like to know more about how the infection works.

Will There Be a Sequel to Godzilla Minus Zero?

This is the big one. After two Godzilla films, Yamazaki has established himself as one of the best directors to ever tackle the big guy, but will there be a third entry in the series? Yamazaki has said he’s “fifty-fifty” on coming back for another film, so it’s not a guarantee. That said, Minus Zero ends on a note that could be developed down the line: the Shikishimas on the run from the US military, who want Noriko back so they can use Godzilla as a weapon. The thematic throughline of Minus Zero – that it is possible to sacrifice too much for the sake of an abstract “greater good” – is paid off by Kōichi and Noriko changing their minds about leaving Akiko at an orphanage for her safety and instead taking her with them to keep the family together, so it’s still a satisfying ending to this story. But with them riding off into the sunset, we can’t help but wonder: how far will the occupiers go to get Noriko back? Is there another adventure in showing the Shikishimas as fugitives staying one step ahead of a colonizing force who want to turn a country’s greatest trauma against the rest of the world?

A sequel to Minus Zero (Godzilla Plus One?) would also give an opportunity to dig deeper into the other threads we’ve discussed. What does Yamazaki’s version of post-war Japan look like in the 1950s? Are there other monsters from the Godzilla franchise that could be revamped in this style? Could a third movie be even louder in IMAX? Honestly, Godzilla is an endless well for potential reinvention, so we hope to see many more movies about him in the years to come.

What were your biggest questions coming out of Godzilla Minus Zero? Let us know in the comments!

articles.title: EA HQ Graced With 'Save Mass Effect' Truck as N7 Day Looms
articles.summary: Mass Effect fans have taken their mission to save BioWare and its beloved sci-fi franchise to EA headquarters with a truck displaying the #SaveMassEffect message.
articles.body:
Mass Effect fans have taken their mission to save BioWare and its beloved sci-fi franchise to EA headquarters with a truck displaying the #SaveMassEffect message.

The latest update to what has ballooned into a full-blown movement arrived today when the dedicated group of fans known as We are Mass Effect announced they had brought their latest billboard right to the publisher's front door. Where their last push arrived in the form of a daylong billboard in New York City's Times Square , this mobile effort will see a truck sharing the word on the streets surrounding EA and EA Sports HQ in Redwood City, California.

Anyone who visits the area today can spot the truck, which features signage updated with a handy QR code and website URL directing curious players to SaveMassEffect.com . The goal, as We are Mass Effect's Mer told IGN, is to "spread the word and bring as much attention to the movement as possible, " but putting it in EA's front lawn after the publisher put Mass Effect games on hold and shuttered BioWare also sends a message of its own.

🚨 WE ARE BACK ON THE STREETS Together with @kalaelizabeth, our first mobile billboard is now outside EA's HQ and EA Sports HQ. 📸 If you're nearby, send us pictures! Please don't enter EA's property. #SaveMassEffect — We are Mass Effect - #SaveMassEffect (@WeAreMassEffect) November 6, 2026

🚨 WE ARE BACK ON THE STREETS Together with @kalaelizabeth, our first mobile billboard is now outside EA's HQ and EA Sports HQ. 📸 If you're nearby, send us pictures! Please don't enter EA's property. #SaveMassEffect

"Social media can sometimes make devastating events feel distant or abstract," We are Mass Effect told IGN when asked about the truck. "It’s easy to read about these news online without fully grasping the human impact behind it. So we wanted to bring the movement into the physical world and make that support visible. We want to remind people that real people have been impacted by the closure of BioWare and the cancellation of the game. We wanted to show them that there is a community that deeply cares about the legacy they’ve created. For us this has never been just about the IP but the people behind it and their work."

Driving a truck around EA HQ will certainly gather some attention, but detractors have warned that no amount of momentum will get the publisher to budge. The goal, as We are Mass Effect has outlined, is not only to offer a message of unity for those who love BioWare franchises like Mass Effect or Dragon Age, but to raise awareness about the human beings affected by these changes, too.

Another mobile billboard will appear near BioWare's former offices tomorrow, with the final billboard launching during The Game Awards next month. Billboard organizer, fundraiser, and content creator Kala Elizabeth told IGN the plan is to drive it around the TGA ceremony for around four hours.

"For me, after our billboards are up, I plan to support the devs however possible and bring visibility to anything else that we can support, but as of right now, I don't have any plans to crowdfund more billboards because these were already exhausting," Elizabeth added with a laugh.

Our first #SaveMassEffect mobile billboard is outside of EA HQ and EA Sports HQ in Redwood! Go get a picture! (do not go into EA if you do) — Kala Elizabeth #SaveMassEffect (@kalaelizabeth) November 6, 2026

Our first #SaveMassEffect mobile billboard is outside of EA HQ and EA Sports HQ in Redwood! Go get a picture! (do not go into EA if you do)

Meanwhile, We are Mass Effect said it is currently putting the finishing touches on a video featuring Mass Effect fans, actors, and contributors for N7 Day tomorrow, November 7. Included in the lineup are Commander Shepard actors Jennifer Hale and Mark Meer. The group is also pushing N7 Play Day in an attempt to boost Steam player numbers for Mass Effect: Legendary Edition .

"And, as a fun throwback to 2012, we’re planning to send cupcakes decorated in N7 colors to EA’s headquarters in Redwood City next week," the group said. "There’s a lot happening, and we don’t plan on stopping anytime soon. The response from the community has shown us just how much Mass Effect and BioWare’s legacy mean to people, and we want to continue finding creative ways to make that support visible."

EA closed down BioWare weeks ago, but as fans get ready for N7 Day, they've done anything but go gently into the night. In addition to that Times Square billboard, a petition urging EA to allow the franchise to live in some capacity has gained more than 300,000 signatures . Save Mass Effect graffiti was also reportedly spray-painted outside of an EA office building in Madrid , while another was decorated with tombstones featuring shuttered studios .

"People are upset, not only about what happened to BioWare, but about the many studios, IPs, and talented devs that have gone through the same thing," We are Mass Effect added. "What we can do is to encourage them to keep supporting the initiatives that the community are organizing, and to keep showing up. We don't want this to become another story, another beloved IP that is forgotten. The most important thing is to make sure people continue paying attention and understand just how much these games and the devs behind them mean to so many."

Mass Effect N7 Wearable LED Helmet Images

"I think the most important thing is supporting the devs and showing that we care," Elizabeth said. "N7 Day is a huge day for Mass Effect and this year is very different. It's important that we're loud and show our support. Signing the petition, using the hashtag, and amplifying the voices of the devs."

A new documentary that filmed the studio's final years was announced just yesterday. While fans hope to make a difference at EA's front door, the publisher is still pushing merchandise for the paused franchise for N7 Day . Meanwhile, a Canadian politician has recently joined the fight .

articles.title: Water Temple Dungeon Walkthrough - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains
articles.body:
Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains the same, there's plenty of new differences to be found while exploring Hyrule. Zora Domain has frozen over, plunging the realm into the deep freeze and drying up the once vast waters of Lake Hylia. Link will need to descend to the Water Temple below the lakebed to undo this curse while seeking out the Sage of Water.

Equipped with a new Zora Tunic and Iron Boots to take him below the watery depths of Lake Hylia, Link will have everything he needs to enter the new Water Temple that can be seen at the bottom of the lake. This can be done by using the hookshot on the target in the remains of lakebed to open the door to the temple.

New to the remake, you'll be able to swap between Iron Boots and swimming normally just by tapping down on the D-Pad, which will come in handy for quickly navigating this dungeon's underwater depths.

Take off the boots as you enter to swim up to the platform above, and you'll be met with an impressive entrance scene. The main room is comprised of a large pagoda-like tower stretching several stories down, with the water risen all the way up to this top floor.

Navigating this dungeon will require a lot of puzzle-solving related to the water, but more importantly, you'll need to find ways to change the water level, as several doors and platforms can only be reached when water levels are at a specific height.

Snipe any pesky Tektites in the way as you swim over to the pagoda and look around. Most of the paths here are inaccessible -- a hookshot target to the north that's too far away, and a locked door to the west. The most interesting path includes a sealed gate blocking access to a familiar looking mural to the east along with an enticing chest.

Making that your first order of business, swap on the Iron Boots and descend downward. You can't enter the pagoda from below yet, and many doors have no landing for you to stand on. Instead, sink all the way down to floor 1F, and watch out for rolling enemies called Spikes -- so named for their ability to extend giant metal spikes when you approach as they roll toward you. Thankfully, even underwater, you can shield against their attack to stun their spikes back into their body, and follow up with a Hookshot to defeat them.

Look for a doorway with two glowing blue pillars, and note the icon above, which displays three tiers and only the bottom tier lit up with blue light. This is your indication that the room leads to a way to lower the water level, so head inside.

It's here you'll be reunited with your "fiancee", Princess Ruto of the Zora! She's here for the same reason as you, to put a stop to Ganondorf's evil and save her people from a frozen death. She's been unable to locate the creature infesting this temple, but an insignia of the Royal Family may provide a clue that only you can solve, so she'll leave things in your hands and swim off.

Once she departs, follow the blue glowing lights up to the top floor by unequipping your Iron Boots, and you'll find a large Treasure Chest with the Dungeon Map you spied behind the bars earlier!

Next, inspect the mural on the wall nearby, which holds the Royal Family insignia with the Triforce. Play Zelda's Lullaby here, and it will trigger a shift in the Water Temple, lowering the water levels down to floor F1!

With the water level receded, hop down the pit to land in a small pool of water back on Floor 1F. Now that the place is dry, you may notice two unlit brazier opposite a lit torch. You can aim your Fairy Bow through the torch to hit the other two with fire arrows (or flex on hitting both braziers with Din's Fire) to open the sealed door to the east.

This room will lock behind you, forcing you into combat with three Spikes. Play defensive and block their assault, then quickly slice them apart when they retract. Doing so will reveal a small Treasure Chest in the room holding your first Small Key.

There's a couple directions to go from here, but you can't get back up to the top floor to open the locked door on 3F -- at least not yet. Instead, stay at ground level and look around. Look for a cracked wall on the south side of the pagoda, and blast it open to find a passage down to the west.

Equip your Iron Boots to descend down to floor B1, and you'll be met with an angry clam called a Shell Blade. Like the Spikes, underwater combat here is all about remaining defensive with your shield out until you can spot a moment to attack with your Hookshot. Block its charge, and wait for the clam to open wide and expose its innards before firing off your Hookshot to take it out.

Swim upwards past the Shell Blade to climb some steps over to a switch, raising a statue that holds a Hookshot target to send you over the gap. There's two Tektites below another pair of Hookshot targets, but your real worry should be the Like Like waiting above.

If you want to play it safe, just hit it with your Fairy Bow to remove the threat from afar. This is not a good time to get eaten and have your items stolen, as unlike the original Ocarina of Time, the Zora Domain shop is sealed up meaning you won't be able to get a replacement Zora Tunic if you lose it! If the Like Like does swallow you, immediately kill it to get anything you lost back!

When the Like Like is defeated, you'll be awarded with another large Treasure Chest that holds the Compass!

Return the way you came to the room with the pagoda. There's one more optional area to check out, which you can do by heading west of the pagoda tower to push a large stone block forward until it falls into a pool below.

Put on your Iron Boots to drop in after it and be ready to deal with another Shell Blade here, then swim up to an opening to the north. There's a small Treasure Chest on a high ledge, but not close enough to reach.

Instead, hop into the water and get ready to fine-tune your Iron Boot usage. A large whirlpool will send you in circles in this pool of water, and you'll want to carefully descend to land on a narrow serpent-like platform next to a statue of the serpent's head. The head holds a switch in its mouth, and hitting it with the Hookshot will open a nearby underwater gate.

Alternate putting your boots on and off to get enough movement to float over through the gate and out of the whirlpool. Keep your boots on when you pass the threshold, as you'll have two more Shell Blades here to contend with. When they've been defeated, swim up the far side to find a platform to climb onto holding the chest with another Small Key.

Since you can't reach the locked door to the north of the pagoda tower, it's time to enter the tower itself using the locked door with the green pillars on either side. Inside the base of the tower, you can look up to find a target to Hookshot to to head upward, onto a ledge with another mural where you can play Zelda's Lullaby, raising the water level to 2F!

With the water level risen, note that a floating block inside the tower has risen up with you, leaving behind a hole leading down to the basement level. Put on your Iron Boots and descend down to the bottom, where three Spikes are waiting.

Once they've been defeated, aim your Hookshot at the green switch above you to open a gate on a low ceiling nearby, dropping down a Shell Blade you'll need to deal with. Once it's gone, swim up the newly opened gate to find an underwater chamber with a small Treasure Chest holding a Red Rupee.

In this small underwater chamber in the basement level below the pagoda tower room, be sure to check around the walls here to find the first of several Gold Skulltulas, which you can defeat with your Hookshot and claim its token.

Swim back up the pagoda tower to exit outside thanks to the floating block in front of the door (there's another spider in here you'll have to leave for later). Outside on floor 2F, you'll have a few options on where to explore next.

Start by swimming back over to where you met Princess Ruto to the east, using the Iron Boots to drop down to the bottom level. You may remember there was a cracked wall halfway up to the top level where you drained the water, and while you can't swim all the way up, the wall is sitting high and dry, with a ledge to plant a bomb at.

On the other side, you'll find a room of Shell Blades you can slice up with your sword, and then inspect the wall behind you for a Gold Skulltula trying to hide.

Next, swim back up to the water line east of the pagoda to find another alcove with a cracked wall you can bomb, opening a path to the northeast. Put the Iron Boots on to sink down to the passage, and here there are several Stingers here underwater -- same as the ones you fought in Jabu-Jabu's belly that like to swarm and dive bomb, but you can Hookshot them after blocking their dive.

Take the Iron Boots off on the far end to end up in a room with a large geyser at the end reaching up to an alcove. There's a switch in a small pool of water nearby you can hit with your Hookshot to lower the geyser. Step on and hit it again to ascend upward, and in the alcove you'll find another small Treasure Chest with a Small Key.

With your two small keys, swim around to the other side of the pagoda tower to the west side, where the line of floating blocks has lined up to lead to a locked door with red glowing pillars, signaling a water level change mural is near.

Inside the next hall is another geyser you can lower by hitting the switch, though it will also bring down an angry Tektite with it. Defeat it, then stand on the platform before hitting the switch again with a ranged shot to ride it up to floor 3F, putting you in front of the final water level-changing mural.

Play Zelda's Lullaby to bring the water up to Floor 3F, bringing you full circle (but with an extra small key this time)!

As you hop down to the pagoda tower platform below, look back to the ledge you jumped from. There's a gust of straw up there, and if you play the Scarecrow's Song, you'll be able to summon Pierre to quickly get back to that mural to change the water level as needed.

Head west once again to the second locked door along the floating platforms. This leads to a long room with a pit in the middle, in which moving platforms on the far side continually move toward the middle and sink into the pit below.

Deal with the nearby Keese first, then carefully slide down this side of the pit onto a moving platform. It will alternate moving up and down, so line up a shot with the targets on each of the far moving platforms to cross the pit.

You'll need to quickly move along the platforms before they drop too far, but you can take a breather on a stationary platform to the side.

There's even some Fairy Writing here, and a note about wanting to beat the humidity with a but of sunbeams means you can play the Sun's Song to get healed by fairy essence!

From the stationary platform, wait for the highest platform to get in range to zip to, and then quickly zip up to the ledge above to get out of the pit.

In the room beyond, you'll find a large room with high platforms over looking a watery pit below filled with Tektites. You can snipe them from afar with your Fairy Bow so they don't hassle you if you accidentally fall down later.

To get across, aim for the blue switch in the middle of the room to raise the various statues around here -- all with Hookshot targets. Zip across the closest one to the west, but don't Hooskhot the target on the statue to the north afterward, or you'll just fall down into the pit below.

Instead, hit the switch again to lower the statue, that way you can zip across to the target to the left of the statue and get past it on the narrow alcove.

Hit the switch again to raise the statues, allowing you to zip to the northeast one leading up to a high ledge. Since you need help getting up to the ledge, hit the switch two more times to bring the statue down so you can jump on top, then ride it upwards. Be sure to break all the pots here for any extra items, and then head inside.

This large foreboding room is more like an endless shallow lake, with a single tree on a small patch of land the only point of interest. Are you even really inside the temple anymore? It's hard to see...

Run past to the far side of the "room", only to find the way forward sealed. As you turn around, you'll spot that an opponent is waiting for you by the tree.

Dark Link as he's known is a nearly exact copy of Link, but filled with evil magic. This means he can match you in a lot of ways, and yet still surprise you if you aren't careful, so take this fight very seriously!

Using his own version of the Master Sword, Dark Link will usually perform three hit slashes, with the last attack in his combo having a red trail on. This is one of the main points you need to remember on when to counter-attack, as dodging that last slash will leave Dark Link open for several moments.

Don't try and get pushy with your own moves, as he can deflect them all with his Hylian Shield. Get too sloppy, and Dark Link can even stand on your sword when you try to stab. If you don't shake him off fast, he'll deal a damaging slash as he jumps off.

While Dark Link is ready for most gadgets like your Bow or Hookshot, it is possible to catch him off guard with Din's Fire early on, which can not only deal damage but stun him for a moment and let you press the attack.

However, after he fades into smoke, he'll respawn after a moment, becoming more powerful and wiser to your tricks. At this point, he's more likely to simply backflip away from any slow attacks like Din's Fire or your Spin Attack.

Dark Link becomes a lot more aggressive and tricky in his second phase, usually opting to perform a quick two-hit stab and follow with a jump attack for his third hit. Blocking it will stagger you, so you'll want to be ready to dodge to the side when you see him leap. However, Dark Link can also feint, and put a pause after his first two stab and delaying the jump attack to bait you into attacking while he sidesteps and then jumps.

Several times, he can also feint into a forward roll, and come out charging his sword into a tier 2 spin attack! Other times, he may try to perform two side slashes before holding the blade out to charge up. In either case, immediately backflip away!

The moment he launches his spin attack is the time to race up for your own jump slash. Don't try to match his spin attacks with your own as you'll almost always be too late. Instead, focus entirely on watching for his jump attacks or spins to find a spot to get in and counter with some damage before backing off.

When you deal enough damage, Dark Link will be banished for good, and the mists will dissipate to reveal the normal room. Head on through to find your grand prize: The Longshot! With this upgraded gadget, you can now latch onto targets much further away than with using the Hookshot!

Step onto the platform behind the chest and test out your Longshot on the distant targets over on the high ledge above you. Up here, you'll find a waterfall pit leading down to a cavern path to take all the way back to the entrance of the Temple.

Move carefully along this cavern river, as there are several whirlpools you'll need to avoid. Get caught swimming through one, and you'll be sucked into a pit. Instead, use your Iron Boots to hold your ground until you can reach ledges to climb up and bypass these pits.

Once you've navigated most of the river and the path curves down to the south, be sure to look behind you. There's a Gold Skulltula up high on a cavern pillar, and while hard to see while underwater, you can still target it with your new Longshot to pull the token down while wearing the Iron Boots.

Move through the final two whirlpools by trudging through the center to the southeast corner, and be sure to look around for some ledges just after the whirlpool, as you can find a pot with a Fairy here to catch in a bottle!

From here, stay on the ledge and look for a large gate with an eye target to shoot, and then use your Longshoot to hook across before the gate closes on you, and exit back toward the entrance hall.

Now that you're back in the are with the pagoda tower, the water level should still be up to the third level. Sink back down to the bottom to return to where you met Princess Ruto, and lower the water level down to floor 1F.

You can now re-climb the inside of the pagoda tower, raising the water level, and look up for a high ceiling with targets to hit with your new Longshot.

This time around, there's more to find at the very top of the tower. Since you have your Longshot, you can look up to find a high ceiling target at the very top of the inside of the pagoda tower and zip up to a high platform. Here, you'll find a Gold Skulltula to claim on the other side of the ceiling that was previously out of view!

With the water up to floor 2F, exit onto the pagoda tower's balcony and head to the north side. You can now hit the eye target on the far wall to reveal the distant target your Longshot can now reach, taking you to the northern room.

Here, you can spot a small Treasure Chest behind a fence, so hop into the pool to the left and sink down with the Iron Boots. There's a small opening here with a large stone block, but all you can do from this angle is pull it back all the way.

Hop out of the pool and look to the right of the fence to spot a high waterfall alcove with a target on the ceiling. Longshot to it to fall down to a different part of the underwater area, allowing you to push the stone block north, and unblocking access to the chest holding to the last Small Key.

Return to the pagoda tower room, and this time sink all the way to the bottom of the north side, dropping all the way down into a basement pit heading north.

Swim up to the ledge, and you'll finally be able to reach the far door thanks to your Longshot, and use your last small key to open the locked door.

The large area beyond features a big pool of water covered in Tektites, and water streaming in from several side alcoves that boulders continually roll out of and through the water into two whirlpool pits.

Take out your Fairy Bow to deplete the Tektite population in the room so they can't hassle you as you try to cross. Wait for a boulder to pass before sinking down with the Iron Boots, then unequip them to cross a ledge before re-equipping them and stopping short of the next boulder path. Wait for the second one to cross before swimming up to the ledge and avoiding the whirlpools.

If you didn't kill all the Tektites, make sure none of them are by the ledge so you can haul up quickly, then ready a spin attack to deal with the remnants.

The room beyond features a small pool of water teeming with Stingers floating about, and three cracked walls on the left side. Go fishing by tossing a few bombs into the water, and deflect any who fly up to attack with your shield.

Once the pool is clear, turn your attention to bombing all the nearby walls. The middle wall has a large stone block, and the two on the side allow you to push it from behind and into the pool of water onto a switch, which raises the water up to the high ledge.

Head through to the next area, where you can step on a switch to raise several geyser platforms. There's a few pesky Tektites that may try to interrupt your crossing, so have your Fairy Bow ready.

On the far side, you can spot a big blue Treasure Chest behind a gate. Head through the nearby door to find the waterway the boulders travel through back to the earlier whirlpool room.

Wait until a boulder rolls on buy to dash east and then north toward an alcove with a door, guarded by a Shell Blade. Defeat it, then claim the Boss Key in the next room!

As you return to the watery alcove of rolling boulders, note the small water fall coming from above (not where the boulders are dropping from). There's a Gold Skulltula hiding up above opposite the falls that you'll need to be quick to target before another boulder rolls on by.

Make your way back to the pagoda tower room one last time. For an easy shortcut, head to the southwest corner and play the Scarecrow Song to summon Pierre up on the third floor ledge where the mural is to raise the water level (otherwise you'll need to head through the red door).

Return to the water level to floor 3F, and head to the north side of the pagoda tower. Use your Longshot on the far target to reach the high ledge, and continue toward the boss door.

The road to the boss door is a bit tricky -- it's a long upward slope with water rushing down from above, and spike traps bouncing from side to side. Equip your Iron Boots to get some footing, and then slowly and carefully forge up the slope, angling yourself to skirt around the spikes as you go. One at the top, steel yourself for another big fight, and head inside.

A wild and unorthodox opponent, the Giant Aquatic Amoeba, Morpha, is a gelatinous ooze of a boss that shouldn't be underestimated. Your on its territory, and that means being extra cautious around water!

Somewhat similar to the Flare Dancers of the Fire Temple, the actual body you need to target is the strange little core that hides in the elongated goopy creature you see before you. And just like those Flare Dancers, your Longshot will be key to exposing its weak point!

Getting it exposed is no easy task, as Morpha will use the waterways around the four major platforms to sneak around you, making it difficult to target. When it does appear, it will soon slam down and try to crush you, so you'll need to react fast and get away. Don't even bother trying to sink down into the water, as you have no means of hurting it while submerged.

Instead, stay mobile and keep moving around the platforms when Morpha appears. It will slam up to three times in a row, changing its position to track you, but then have a moment it needs to recover afterward. Turn back and ready your Longshot to pull it out of the goop, and get to slashing with your sword!

After taking several hits, Morhpa will bounce around and seek out water to get away from you. You can try to get in a few more hits, but don't get too absorbed in your task that you leave yourself open.

Soon after getting back into the water, Morpha will reform its gelatinous arm, and start to sweep wide circles around where it appears. This can happen fast, and the best way to quickly avoid this sweeping attack is to target one of the Longshot points along each wall, to zip away to safety. Morpha will still move along the water as it spins, which is why zipping into the air can really help you get some distance.

If you get caught by its spinning attack, Morpha will wrap around and constrict you, dealing heavy damage if you don't break free quickly by mashing you attack buttons!

Wait for Morpha to stop spinning an exhaust itself, then race back over to the platforms it draped itself on to Longshot the body out of its goop, and repeat the process of slashing it apart.

After taking enough damage, Morpha will play dirty in its next phase, and appear within a tendril somewhere in the arena, but also raising up tendrils all along the water in every corner. This makes it hard to track its actual spot, and you'll also need to dodge the slams every stray appendage as you make your way toward the core!

Once you spot it, bait it into slamming down to extract the core and keep slashing away. If you don't kill it here, it may come back with extra appendages to perform its spinning attack again, so be careful!

Keep using your Longshot to pull Morhpa's core to a safe spot to slash it apart, and the creature will soon wither and die, leaving you with a new Heart Container as the water drains out of the arena!

Enter the blue light, and you'll be transported back to the Chamber of Sages. Your new Sage of Water will be there to meet you, though unfortunately it looks like the wedding might have to be postponed. A bittersweet parting, but Princess Ruto will stand firm in her resolve to take the fight to Ganondorf, and add her strength to yours by bestowing yet another gift to Link, the Water Medallion.

With the destruction of the creature fouling the waters, the curse will lift on Zora Domain, breaking away much of the ice and restoring water flow to Lake Hylia, completely filling up the mighty lake once more! Sheik will congratulate you on your endeavors thus far, before making another stealthy retreat.

Before you head out to the next temple, be sure to inspect the large plaque by the pedestal for the temple. You've fulfilled the prophecy of restoring the waters to the lake, and the sun should be rising any moment.

Take aim at the rising sun to the east, and fire your bow when the light hits the sky brilliantly. Some of that light will fall to the earth, in the form of a brand new upgrade! Swim to the small island to obtain the Fire Arrows! With this, you can supercharge your Fairy Bow to shoot elemental arrows (without needing to fire a regular arrow through a torch), and can deal incredible damage at the cost of a lot of your magic power.

Up Next: Biggest Changes and Differences

As part of the AliExpress early Black Friday sale, you can get it for as low as $131.79 with free shipping after you apply $30 off coupon code " DBDEAL30 ". It sells for $249 on Amazon . The Adventurer 5M offers great performance at at outstanding budget price. I would say it is the best 3D printer priced below $150. The 5M is easy to setup, produces great 3D prints with minimal fiddling, and offers plenty of add-on mods including a kit that fully encloses the chamber and another that adds a camera .

Flashforge Adventurer 3D Printer Drops to $131

Make sure you're signed into your account to see the shipping options (may need to refresh twice )

FlashForge Adventurer 5M CoreXY 3D Printer

The Adventurer 5M is Flashforge's least expensive CoreXY printer. In fact, it's one of the least expensive CoreXY printers from any well-regarded brand, but with upgrades where they matter. For starters, the Adventurer 5M features a CoreXY structure typically found in pricier models. In a CoreXY printer, only the print head moves while the motors are permanently fixed. Since the motors are generally the heaviest component, this improves print speed and precision.

The open bed has a build volume measuring approximately 8.7" cubed. A closed chamber offers a more controlled environment that eliminates unpredicatable variables like dust or wind and stabilizes temperatures for consistent result. Usually this costs a premium, but FlashForge sells a kit that converts the open bed into a closed chamber for $39.99 . If you want to spend even less and don't care about aesthetics, you can just put a big box over it and call it a day.

The 5M boasts a print speed of up to 600mm/s with 20,000mm/s² acceleration and can print a benchy in 14 minutes. The high-flow 32mm³/s nozzle with 280°C direct extruder can warm up to 200°C in as fast as 35 seconds for consistent filament dispensing. Build quality is solid since all of the structural components are made of metal. The 4.3" color touchscreen control panel is intuitive to use with minimal fiddling and the 5M supports essential features such as auto leveling and vibration compensation. Assembly is quick and easy and you'll be able to print your first object in minutes.

articles.body:
Gift of Improved Spin is a permanent upgrade in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. This upgrade makes your spin attack permanently emit a wave of magic power. This upgrade is obtained at the Hyrule Castle Great Fairy Fountain. This guide will teach you how to get Gift of Improved Spin, including requirements and location.

Check out IGN's guide on Gift of Improved Spin below:

Gift of Improved Spin is bestowed at the Great Fairy Fountain outside of Hyrule Castle. You may have noticed this cracked rock wall on your way to meet Zelda at the start of the game. Once you have obtained the Bombs, you can return and destroy the wall to gain access to the Great Fairy Fountain.

Inside the fountain, stand on the Triforce symbol in front of the water and play Zelda's Lullaby to summon the Great Fairy. She will demand an offering of 50 Rupees. Pay up and you will get Gift of Improved Spin.

Gift of Halved Damage is a permanent upgrade in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. This upgrade permanently reduces all damage received by half. This upgrade is obtained at the Ganondorf's Castle Great Fairy Fountain. This guide will teach you how to get Gift of Halved Damage, including requirements and location.

Check out IGN's guide on Gift of Halved Damage below:

Gift of Halved Damage is bestowed at the Great Fairy Fountain outside Ganondorf's Castle. Right of the entrance to Ganondorf's Castle you will see this black pillar with gold symbols on it. This pillar cannot be moved until you have the Golden Gauntlets from inside Ganondorf's Castle.

articles.title: Why You Should Be Playing Queen's Domain, the Old-School RPG Inspired by King's Field - IGN
articles.summary: Queen's Domain impressions by Michael Higham, played on PC (also available on PS5, Xbox, and Switch 2)"I'm a sucker for a good throwback to the early polygonal 32-bit era – Mouthwashing, Signalis, Crow Country, and Boltgun 2 are some recent favorites that come to mind. The latest one I've locked in on is Queen's Domain, a fantasy RPG that's as if an Elder Scrolls game was made for the PlayStation 1. Actually, it's explicitly inspired by FromSoftware's pre-Dark Souls series King's Field, where slow, deliberate first-person combat and exploration complemented punishing difficulty (which would later become FromSoft's signature, of course). But as much as Queen's Domain draws clear inspiration or shares similarities, it's a singular experience in 2026 that, from what I've played so far, wields the intended friction of an old-school game wonderfully."
articles.body:
Queen's Domain impressions by Michael Higham, played on PC (also available on PS5, Xbox, and Switch 2)

"I'm a sucker for a good throwback to the early polygonal 32-bit era – Mouthwashing, Signalis, Crow Country, and Boltgun 2 are some recent favorites that come to mind. The latest one I've locked in on is Queen's Domain, a fantasy RPG that's as if an Elder Scrolls game was made for the PlayStation 1. Actually, it's explicitly inspired by FromSoftware's pre-Dark Souls series King's Field, where slow, deliberate first-person combat and exploration complemented punishing difficulty (which would later become FromSoft's signature, of course). But as much as Queen's Domain draws clear inspiration or shares similarities, it's a singular experience in 2026 that, from what I've played so far, wields the intended friction of an old-school game wonderfully."

articles.title: All Deku-Stick Bag Upgrade Locations - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Deku-Stick Bag determines how many Deku Sticks you can carry at a time in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. By default you can hold 10 Deku Sticks,
articles.body:
Deku-Stick Bag determines how many Deku Sticks you can carry at a time in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. By default you can hold 10 Deku Sticks, but this capacity can be quickly upgraded to 30.

Check out IGN's full guide to Deku-Stick Bag upgrades below.

The overall amount of Deku Sticks you can carry can be upgraded twice in Ocarina of Time, and you can earn both upgrades fairly quickly. Each upgrade will bring you through The Lost Woods.

For the first upgrade, enter the Lost Woods from Kokiri Forest and immediately head to the left, past a Skull Kid playing on a stump, and through a tunnel to a spot overlooking the bridge leading to Hyrule Field.

On this path, by the bridge, you’ll discover a Business Scrub, who’ll attack you by firing Deku Nuts at you. Deflect the projectile using your Deku Shield, and it’ll soon surrender. You’ll then be able to purchase a Deku Stick capacity upgrade for 40 Rupees, which will increase your maximum inventory space from 10 to 20.

For the second upgrade, you’ll first need to borrow the Skull Mask from the Happy Mask Shop in Castle Town. Then, head over to Lost Woods and search for a meadow.

Hidden within it, you’ll be able to locate the hidden grotto full of Deku Scrubs. Equip the Skull Mask, and they’ll immediately swarm you with excitement. The leader of the Deku Scrubs will then offer you the capacity upgrade, free of charge. This upgrade will increase your inventory space further by another 10 spaces, allowing you to hold up to 30 total Deku Sticks.

Check out IGN's full guide to Deku-Seed Bag upgrades below.

In order to fire more Deku Seeds from your slingshot, you can track down these bag locations in any order you choose. One them requires you to play the Shooting Gallery minigame in Castle Town. If you win the game with a perfect score, your maximum capacity will be increased to carry 40 seeds.

If you did the minigame first, the second upgrade can be found in Lost Woods. Locate the hanging target (most easily found by entering the Lost Woods from Kokiri Forest and making an immediate right turn), and shoot the center three times in a row. Upon doing so, a Deku Scrub will appear and reward you with another upgrade, further increasing your capacity to 50 seeds.

articles.title: Avengers: Doomsday Car Commercial Features New Look at Nightcrawler, Sparks Theories About Unannounced Heroes
articles.summary: An Avengers: Doomsday car commercial just revealed a first look at Alan Cumming's Nightcrawler in motion – and it may have teased a surprising cameo, too.
articles.body:
An Avengers: Doomsday car commercial just revealed a first look at Alan Cumming's Nightcrawler in motion – and it may have teased a surprising cameo, too.

Marvel Studios has played it safe when it comes to big reveals for next month's all-star superhero movie. As it marks the beginning of the end of the Multiverse saga and a proper introduction for Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom, it makes sense that we've not seen too much yet, but a new Jeep commercial is changing that.

The car brand got in on the hype with a crossover commercial for Jeep 4x4s today. While similar videos are far from a new concept, it goes the extra mile by sending its cars through an onslaught of superhero antics themed around Avengers: Doomsday. It's not exactly footage from the movie, but between shots of Human Torch flyovers and shots of a war-torn X-Men school, Marvel did allow a first look at elements official trailers have hidden from viewers thus far.

New Jeep ad for ‘AVENGERS: DOOMSDAY’ Featuring Doctor Doom, Captain America, Thor, Johnny Storm, Nightcrawler, Cyclops, Sentinels, The Thing and H.E.R.B.I.E. — Cosmic Marvel (@cosmic_marvel) November 6, 2026

New Jeep ad for ‘AVENGERS: DOOMSDAY’ Featuring Doctor Doom, Captain America, Thor, Johnny Storm, Nightcrawler, Cyclops, Sentinels, The Thing and H.E.R.B.I.E.

Cumming's Kurt Wagner, a.k.a. Nightcrawler, is one character who was announced to be in the film ages ago, but we've seen so little of him so far . For some reason, this Jeep commercial marks our first official look at Nightcrawler using his teleportation powers in Avengers: Doomsday since 2003's X2 . Although it's a quick moment that shows him leaping through cars, it's still nice to see him considered worth highlighting amongst such a jam-packed lineup of stars.

Again, it's hard to read too much into a car commercial , but when The Thing, Thor, and Sentinels are featured so prominently, it's also hard to ignore. So, while Nightcrawler does get the spotlight here, it makes sense that there's little to cling to in terms of story details. Well, except for one thing.

Warning! Potential spoilers for Avengers: Doomsday follow.

Marvel fans love to dig into the details of any official communication from Marvel, and today's Jeep commercial is no different. As the Jeeps park toward the end of the video, they return to one location via those all-too-familiar magical portals we've seen in the Marvel Cinematic Universe so many times before. From the Doctor Strange movies to Avengers: Endgame, these orange circles have offered heroes transport before. The reason this has comic book movie fans restless today is that Benedict Cumberbatch's Doctor Strange is one of the few heroes not confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday yet.

The portals just confirmed Dr. Strange will be in Doomsday. — AdnaanJnr (@AdnaanJnr) November 6, 2026

The portals just confirmed Dr. Strange will be in Doomsday.

@DiscussingFilm hold up I see dr strange portals at the end 👀 — Gabe ☘️⚡️ (@CelticsGotNext) November 6, 2026

@DiscussingFilm hold up I see dr strange portals at the end 👀

In fact, other magic users like Wong and Ned Leeds haven't been confirmed to be in the cast either. As many have pointed out, there's a decent chance this is little more than a convenient tie-in to bring the Jeep commercial's multiverse message together. Arguments to the contrary point out that other heroes and abilities are pretty accurately represented here.

"I wonder if the Strange portals mean anything," one Reddit user wondered .

"Will Jeep return in Avengers: Secret Wars?" another joked .

Would Marvel have included portals if they weren't going to be featured in Avengers: Doomsday? It's hard to say, but it's also more Doctor Strange-like wizardry than we've seen in any official footage thus far. Who knows? Maybe it's Doctor Doom who's learned the power of the magic portals.

D23 First Look Avengers: Doomsday Costumes and Props

We'll have to wait until Avengers: Doomsday comes to theaters December 18 to see if there's anything to these latest MCU theories. In the meantime, you can check out Downey and Pedro Pascal's Halloween costumes , which also happened to spark a round of theories . You can also see how a Dunkin' ad revealed an updated accent for Channing Tatum's Gambit .

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

articles.title: Robert Pattinson Reportedly Screen-Tested for 007 in James Bond 26
articles.summary: Robert Pattinson reportedly screen-tested for the role of 007 in James Bond 26. Lex Luthor actor Nicholas Hoult has also emerged as a contender for the role of Bond.
articles.body:
Robert Pattinson reportedly screen-tested for the role of 007 in James Bond 26 .

"The screen tests are said to have occurred the weekend of Oct. 24," according to The Hollywood Reporter . "THR previously reported that four, possibly five actors were in the mix but only three names surfaced at the time."

Those three named actors are Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and Josh O’Connor .

THR also said Lex Luthor actor Nicholas Hoult has emerged as a contender for the role of Bond.

This wouldn't be the first time Hoult and Pattinson have vied for the same high-profile franchise role. Hoult was the runner-up for the role of Batman in Matt Reeves’ 2022 film, which Pattinson won.

Meanwhile, Variety claims that "Harry Styles has had discussions about the part, and Theo James also hasn’t been ruled out."

It’s unusual but not unheard of for an actor to lead two big franchises at the same time. Harrison Ford played Han Solo and Indiana Jones in the same era, later adding Jack Ryan to the mix. Robert Downey Jr. starred in the Sherlock Holmes films while anchoring the MCU as Iron Man.

Pattinson recently worked with James Bond 26 director Denis Villeneuve on Dune: Part 3. The Bond screen tests took place in London where Pattinson is currently filming The Batman: Part 2.

At 40 years old, Pattinson is older than the three other named 007 contenders and Hoult, who are all 36 years old. As someone who launched to global fame with the Twilight films, Pattinson is a far cry from the "fresh face" that producers were reportedly looking to cast at one point.

For more 007 coverage, take a look back at how the media has reacted to the casting of the James Bond actors .

What do you think of Robert Pattinson possibly being both Batman and James Bond? Let us know in the comments.

Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.

articles.title: World of Warcraft Forever World First Level 60 Character Hits Cap Three Days After Launch
articles.summary: World of Warcraft Forever World First Level 60 Character Hits Cap Three Days After Launch
articles.body:
World of Warcraft Forever is all about taking your time and exploring the world, rather than rushing to the endgame. But, despite the Forever team's insistence on taking your time and making friends, a WoW Forever player has already hit level 60.

Team JokerD, led by the eponymous streamer was the first team of characters to hit level 60, and the team was made up entirely of Undead characters and one Troll. The Undead race was important there, because Blizzard changed the Cannibalize ability to help you regenerate mana, which meant there was little to no downtime between massive pulls. I spent some time watching the streams of these speedrunners, and they'd gather entire groups of mobs to nuke them down with AoE abilities.

JokerD's claim to fame was being the world's first level 60 when World of Warcraft Classic launched back in 2019, so it's not super suprising that his team was the first to hit max level in Forever. There was plenty of competition this time around, but JokerD's team was pretty far ahead of the fray throughout the entire race. Even at the time of writing, the second place character who's not part of JokerD's team is Ksuper Worldfirst, who is still level 53.

However, while it's cool that these players have been able to hit max level already, there's not much of a reason to rush to endgame right now. The first raids, Barrow Deeps, Hyjal Summit and Onyxia's Lair, don't open until December 9, so players hitting level cap this weekend might find it hard to find what they should do next.

When I interviewed WoW Forever principal game designer Kris Zierhut , he made it pretty clear that Blizzard intends players to level multiple characters, and reinforced that leveling is a major part of the game. So, if you do manage to make it to level 60 super early and you run out of content before raids open, it might be worth it to start another character and take a different path to max level.

WoW Forever also had an extremely smooth launch , and was largely free of any major server problems. But, then again, Blizzard later came out and bragged that the game was running on more than 200TB of RAM, so it'd be a little concerning if the servers still buckled under the weight of players trying to log in.

Just like the other Deku gear, both Deku-Nut Bag upgrades are found in the Lost Woods. The first upgrade is located in a grotto at the very end of the Lost Woods, next to the doorway to Sacred Grove. You will need the Bombs to clear the boulder and get inside.

If you haven't been there before, it is: right, left, right, left, left from the front entrance . Look in the grass toward the back to find the entrance.

Once in the Forest Stage, get on the pedestal and equip the Mask of Truth. This will cause the Scrubs to get scared. Speak to the Scrub Leader.

He will give you the Biggest Deku-Nut Bag free of charge, upgrading your capacity to 40.

articles.title: How to Get Epona - Malon's Friend Side Quest - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Malon's Friend is a secondary quest you can fulfill in the Threads of Time quest list, and is centered around Lon Lon Ranch, and befriending the horse,
articles.body:
Malon's Friend is a secondary quest you can fulfill in the Threads of Time quest list, and is centered around Lon Lon Ranch, and befriending the horse, Epona, which you can eventually ride. Doing so will require you to visit the ranch several times - once when you are a child, and again when you're an adult.

Though you can visit Lon Lon Ranch in the center of Hyrule Field shortly after leaving Kokiri Forest, there's not much you can do there at first. Instead, you'll need to first meet with Princess Zelda in Hyrule Castle (meeting both Malon and Talon who work at the ranch in the process). After leaving the castle, be sure to head back to the ranch at the earliest opportunity.

Entering the ranch, you should first make your way directly past the buildings and over to the main part of the ranch housing all the horses in a large field (assuming its still daytime). In the middle, you'll find the girl Malon singing her iconic song to a young horse that will bolt away when you draw close.

Malon will introduce you to her "friend", whose name is Epona. Apparently she's very shy, but opens up when she hears the tune Malon sings. Malon will ask if you have and instrument to accompany her with, so oblige by pulling out your Fairy Ocarina. Follow along with her tune:

Enter the prompt, and you'll learn Epona's Song, and the horse will immediately come running!

Note that some Threads of Time, like "Malon's Friend", aren't entirely essential to complete your main story objectives, but are important side quests that you can start at any time, and complete them later in the story.

You can't do anything more with Epona for now since she's too small to ride (as are you), but there are a few other things to take note of in the ranch, including finding some Gold Skulltulas, Heart Pieces, and earning an Empty Bottle by playing a game with Talon.

After collecting all Spiritual Stones and unlocking the Door of Time, you'll return to Hyrule seven years later. Much has changed, but it also means the little horse you befriended has grown as well.

Return back to Lon Lon Ranch to find the place transformed for the worse. Now called Ingo Ranch, the conniving stablehand has curried Ganondorf's favor to take over the place, forcing Malon to work for him as he sells his steeds off to donate all of their money to the new King of Evil, forcing the ranch deeper into debt.

If you come back at night, you'll find Malon alone singing her song quietly at the edge of the field, wishing someone would help her and take her beloved horse Epona away from all this.

While you're here, be sure to inspect the crumbling tower in the corner of the ranch where you once found a Piece of Heart. You can actually hookshot up to the vines and climb the tower to find a small Treasure Chest with a Business Seed.

During the day, take Ingo up on his offer to ride the horses for a 20 Rupee fee. Once your inside the pen, play Epona's Song, and the normally skittish and now fully-grown horse will come galloping over. It's worth taking a minute to get used to the controls - testing how she runs around corners, and jumping over barriers by picking up speed by pressing A to consume carrots (which only replenish after a short time has passed).

Once you're feeling confident, approach Ingo while riding Epona and talk to him. He'll have a wager: one race around the track, and whoever wins get 20 Rupees.

To win, take to the inside of the track, and space out your carrot usage when on the straightaways. Gallop faster after waiting a few moments so your carrots deplete at a steady rate, and you'll leave Ingo in the dust!

Ingo will be so pissed, he'll challenge you to a second race. If he wins, he gets the money, but if you win, you'll get to keep Epona! Ingo will be faster on this attempt, but you may find its still a lot easier than it was in the original game. Be ready to gallop forward on those straight shots, when Ingo will also try and make his move, to ensure you beat him when going around the corners, then blast the remaining carrots to blaze over the finish line!

True to his word, Ingo will let you keep Epona... but he won't let you leave the ranch. Barring the gate, you'll need to find a new way out. Luckily, if you look around the ranch's walls, you can find low fencing in each direction. Just make sure you have plenty of runway to build up speed before pointing Epona at the low walls, and she'll make a mighty leap out of Lon Lon Ranch!

Epona is now officially your trusted steed! This means you can play Epona's Song anywhere in Hyrule Field or Lake Hylia, and she'll come galloping over. Once you have a suitable ranged weapon, you'll even be able to use it on horseback and hunt down Poes!

To help celebrate, be sure to return to Kakariko. By now, the Pocket Cucco you were given will have hatched, and it's time to share the good news with someone who needs to wake up. Head over to Talon in the large home by the center of the village and pull out the Cucco to give him a mighty wake up call.

After telling him to spoke with Ingo and Talon, he'll promise to turn over a new leaf and hurry back. If you head back after him, you'll find that Talon will have taken back control of the ranch after Ingo came to his senses, and things are back to normal!

Be sure to speak with everyone, and Malon will thank you for breaking Epona out, and hopes the two of you will have fun together. She'll now offer an obstacle course race that you can attempt. Race around the track while hopping barriers and dodging obstacles for a fast time. If you complete in under 40 seconds, she'll transport something cool to your home in Kokiri Forest!
